Because the issuer is a Money Service Provider (DAA 4.1(1)), COB 8.2 applies to it (COB 8.1.4), and COB 8.2.16(2)(c) requires money remaining with the firm to be paid to each Client before the general order of winding up; it is not clear whether this covers the reserve, which is not Client Money under COB 8.2.1 and PMS 9.3, and holders who have no client agreement with the issuer (DAA 4.11.2(3)). DAA 4.7.2(3)(b) refers to an issuer "required to implement a redemption plan", but no rule sets out such a plan. Example: if the reserve forms part of the estate and holders rank as unsecured creditors, an issuer with 50 million USD of coins in circulation, a reserve of 50 million USD, no other assets, other unsecured creditors of 10 million USD and winding-up costs of 1 million USD pays holders about 82 cents per coin (49 / 60). The wording of 4.7.1(4), 4.7.3(7) and 4.11.2(1) is close to Articles 36(3), 37 and 39(1) of the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (EU) 2023/1114; Article 36(2) of that Regulation, which requires the reserve to be legally segregated from the issuer's estate so that the issuer's creditors have no recourse to it, has no counterpart in the DAA.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0170 — Bank-cooperation Rules 3.1.1: the USD 1,000 monthly limit is on "depositing", but 3.1.3 and the Guidance treat it as a limit on investments (purchases)
entry.summary: Reported. Rule 3.1.1 requires controls preventing individual Retail Clients resident in Kazakhstan (unless they pass the provider's test) "from depositing more than 1,000 (one thousand) USD within one calendar month". The heading of 3.1 is "Limits for investing", rule 3.1.3 speaks of "the limits on investments in Digital Assets" as provided under rule 3.1.1, and the Guidance says: "Only purchase transactions of Digital Assets in the jurisdiction of the Centre are taken into account when calculating the limit." Deposits and purchases can differ: a client may deposit USD 3,000 and buy for USD 900, or deposit USD 900 and buy for USD 3,000 using sale proceeds.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0169 — Bank-cooperation Rules: Schedule 2 still shows the 2023 DAA capital table (Self-managed Fund row, old DATF measure), while 3.3.1 refers to the DAA rules
entry.summary: Reported. Rule 3.3.1 of the Rules and mechanisms of cooperation with second-tier banks requires Digital Asset Service Providers to hold minimum capital "in accordance with rules 2.2. and 3.2" of the DAA, and 3.3.2 says the amounts "are specified in Schedule 2". Schedule 2, both in the PDF on aifc.kz (approved 11 December 2023) and on the regulator's website, still has (1) the row "Managing a Collective Investment Scheme, which is a Self-managed Fund ..." with USD 200,000, which the DAA no longer contains (it is absent from the consolidated version in force from 1 January 2025), and (2) the old measure for operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility: "sufficient working capital ... in different market conditions (both negative and positive scenarios)". Since 1 January 2026 the DAA uses "operational expenses in fiat currency". The other rows match. It is not clear which source governs.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0168 — REP 3.3(2) cites 'REP 2.2.2' (does not exist) and REP 3.8 cites 'the CIR' (no longer a defined rulebook name)
entry.summary: Reported. (1) 3.3(2): the AFSA may determine fitness 'according to the criteria set out in REP 2.2.2'; REP 2.2 has subrules (1)-(2), the criteria are in REP 2.2(2). (2) 3.8: a Representative Office may only market a Unit of a Foreign Fund 'in accordance with the requirements set out in the CIR'. 'CIR' was the Glossary abbreviation for the Collective Investment Scheme Rules only in Glossary V1 (29.04.2018); from V2 (30.07.2018) to V23 the abbreviation is 'CIS'. Meaning survives by context in both places.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0167 — AUD Annex C (Insurance Intermediary Auditor's Report) measures client money 'in accordance with COB 11', which has no client-money rules
entry.summary: Reported. AUD Annex C (Insurance Intermediary Auditor's Report), paragraphs (a) and (b)(i), measure client money "in accordance with COB 11", while (b)(iii)-(iv) refer to COB 8. The client-money rules for insurance intermediaries were added to COB as section 8.5 in December 2018; COB 11 now ends at 11.7.7 and contains no client-money rules. The meaning can be recovered from (b)(iii)-(iv) and the title of the Annex.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0166 — AUD 9.2.1 table: the rows for Non-Exempt Funds and Reporting Entities refer to CIR 11.4(a) and MAR 3.2.2, which do not require an audit
entry.summary: Reported. The table in AUD 9.2.1 links each auditor's report to the rule that requires it. Two rows do not lead there: "Financial Statements - Non-Exempt Fund" refers to "CIR 11.4(a)", a rulebook name the Glossary no longer has (the fund auditor rule is CIS 10.4), and "Financial Statements - Reporting Entity" refers to MAR 3.2.2, which is "Signing of the annual report" (the audit duty is MAR 3.1.2). The rows for the client asset reports refer to COB 8.2.19, 8.3.14 and 11.8.15, which no longer require an auditor's report; the draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0005 replaces these references with a new GEN 6.3.9, and we support that change, but it leaves the two rows above as they are. In the draft GEN 6.3.9, item (a)(iv) requires an "Insurance Intermediary Auditor's Report" "if the Authorised Firm is permitted to control or hold Client Money". This is the same condition as for the Client Money Auditor's Report in (a)(ii) and is not limited to insurance intermediaries; the Glossary and the AUD table call this report "Insurance Intermediary Audit Report".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0165 — PMS 7.9.2(2) and (4): broken cross-reference "subrule 0" in the refund rule (PDF and regulator's website)
entry.summary: Reported. Both subrules refer to "subrule 0", an unresolved automatic cross-reference; the same "0" appears in the text on the regulator's website. The intended target is 7.9.2(1) (refund of an unauthorised Payment Transaction). The meaning survives by context.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0164 — PMS 9.3(1) defines relevant Client Money 'for the purposes of COB 9.1' - COB 9.1 is Trade confirmations
entry.summary: Reported. PMS 9.3(1): 'For the purposes of COB 9.1. relevant Client Money includes: ...'. COB 9.1 (Reporting to Clients) is 'Trade confirmations'; it does not use the term. The term is used by PMS 9.1(1) ('relevant Client Money in PMS 9.3'), so the intended anchor is PMS 9.1. Meaning survives by context.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0163 — PMS 10.2.1(2)(b)(d): capital deduction of 'defined benefit pension fund assets of the Insurance Intermediary'
entry.summary: Reported. PMS 10.2.1(2)(b) lists deductions from the capital of a Money Service Provider. Item d) deducts "defined benefit pension fund assets of the Insurance Intermediary" - wording taken from the rules for insurance intermediaries. The other items refer to the Money Services Provider. Item h) (assets not readily realisable) probably captures such assets anyway.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0162 — PMS Part 3 application statement can be read as limiting Part 3 to digital-asset money services, although the Part 3 rules address every Money Service Provider
entry.summary: Reported. The opening statement of PMS Part 3 reads: "This Part 3 applies to activities of Providing Money Services in relation to Digital Assets and issuing Fiat stablecoins, except for PMS 3.1 ..., PMS 3.2 ..., 3.4." It can be read as an additional application (Part 3, except 3.1, 3.2 and 3.4, also applies to digital-asset activities), which matches PMS 1.1, the rules addressed to "a Money Service Provider" and the Guidance in DAA Part 4. It can also be read as limiting Part 3 to digital-asset activities. The statement does not mention Commodity stablecoins.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0161 — PMS 2.4.2(1)(c): stablecoin criteria "in subrules (4) or (5)": (5) is a prior notice, and the reserve test in (4)(c) covers only Fiat stablecoins
entry.summary: Reported. PMS 2.4.2(1)(c) requires, for a Fiat or Commodity stablecoin, that "all of the requirements in subrules (4) or (5) as applicable are met". Subrule (4) gives reserve criteria, but its reserve-adequacy test in (4)(c) speaks only of "reserves in respect of Fiat stablecoins". Subrule (5) requires the provider to notify the AFSA at least 10 days before admission; it can be read as a condition of admission, but the text does not say when (5) applies instead of (4). No reserve-adequacy test is stated for Commodity stablecoins. DAA 2.8.2(1)(c) has the same wording (AIFC2-DAA-04).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0160 — PMS 4.3 and 7.3(3) list different cases in which a redemption fee may be charged: may a fee be charged for a redemption during the agreement?
entry.summary: Reported. Two rules govern fees on the redemption of Electronic Money, and both use "only where". PMS 4.3(1) allows a fee where (a) the redemption is requested before the termination of the client agreement, (b) a fixed-term agreement is terminated early, or (c) redemption is requested more than one year after termination. PMS 7.3(3) allows a fee only where it "relates to early termination or late redemption". A redemption requested at early termination meets both rules. A redemption during a running agreement, without termination, is allowed by 4.3(1)(a) and referred to in 4.4(1), but does not fit 7.3(3). Read together, such a fee is not allowed, which leaves little room for 4.3(1)(a).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0159 — aifc.kz DAA page: the "V2 (18 October 2024)" link opens the initial version; the consolidated V4 is listed under "Amendments" and Amendments No. 3 under "Past Version"
entry.summary: Reported. On the aifc.kz page of the AIFC Rules on Digital Asset Activities: (1) the links "AIFC Rules on Digital Asset Activities V2., with amendments as of 4 September 2024, commence on 18 October 2024" and "Initial Version" open the same file. Its cover shows a commencement date of 1 January 2024 and no amendments, so the text in force from 18 October 2024 is not available at that link. (2) Under "Amendments", the entry "A3., with amendments as of 13 April 2025" opens the consolidated version with amendments as of 13 April 2025, while the amending instrument (Amendments No. 3) is listed under "Past Version". (3) No amending instrument dated 4 September 2024 is linked, so the source of changes made between the initial version and the version in force on 1 January 2025 (for example the new lettering of DAA 4.5(1), see AIFC2-DAA-02) cannot be identified from the page.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0158 — DAA 4.2: refusal grounds joined by 'and' - literally the AFSA must refuse only if both general requirements and capital fail
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 4.2 says the AFSA may not grant a licence if "(a) the applicant does not meet general authorisation requirements ..., and (b) the applicant does not have capital of at least USD 200,000". Read literally, the bar applies only when both conditions fail. Rules 2.2 and 3.2 use the positive form ("unless the applicant satisfies all of the following"). The AFSA keeps its general power to refuse, and 4.6.1(2) treats the USD 200,000 as a standing requirement.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0157 — DAA 3.10.2(3)(c) refers twice to 'DAA 2.8.10(1)', which does not exist
entry.summary: Reported. DAA section 2.8 ends at 2.8.8; there is no 2.8.10. The sibling subrules (2) and (3) of the same rule refer to '3.10.2 (1)' (the DASP risk warnings); the DATF equivalent is 2.8.5(1). Meaning survives by context.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0156 — DAA 4.7.4(3)(b)(ii): reserve repos 'with a maturity of 7 or less' - unit missing
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 4.7.4(3)(b)(ii) lists "repurchase agreements with a maturity of 7 or less". The unit is missing; PMS 9.2(d) uses "7 (seven) days or less".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0155 — DAA 4.4(2) in Part 4 (money services / stablecoin issuers) addresses 'a Digital Asset Trading Facility Operator'
entry.summary: Reported. 4.4(2) - the only Board-of-Directors rule in Part 4 - repeats verbatim 2.3.2(1) for a 'Digital Asset Trading Facility Operator', which is regulated by Chapter 2. 4.4(1), (3) and (4) address the Digital Asset Service Provider. Amendments No. 4 edited this very subrule (deleting the one-third independence sentence and its note) and left the addressee unchanged.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0154 — DAA 4.11.3: is the base of the 2% ongoing capital the outstanding stablecoins or the reserve assets?
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 4.11.3(1) sets ongoing capital at 2% "of the average outstanding Fiat stablecoins or Commodity stablecoins". For an issuer with several categories, 4.11.3(3) says this amount "should be the sum of the average amounts of the reserve assets backing each category", and the Guidance describes it as the average amount of reserve assets at the end of each day over the preceding 6 months. Reserve assets must be at least equal to the outstanding stablecoins (4.7.1(2)) and may be larger. For an issuer with one category, the binding text does not say which base applies or over what period the average is taken.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0153 — DAA 4.7.2: annual reserve audit may end 4 months after year end, but its result is due 4 weeks after the 'reference date of the valuation'
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 4.7.2(1) requires the issuer to "mandate an independent third party audit of the reserve assets annually but not later than four months after the close of its financial year"; 4.7.2(2) requires the result to be provided "at the latest within 4 weeks of the reference date of the valuation". "Reference date of the valuation" is not defined, and (1) does not say whether the four months apply to commissioning or to completing the audit. If the reference date is the financial-year end, the result could be due before the audit has to be done.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0152 — DAA 2.8.2(1)(c): stablecoin admission criteria "in (4) or (5)": (5) is a notice after admission, and the reserve test in (4)(c) covers only Fiat stablecoins
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 2.8.2(1)(c) makes admission of a Fiat or Commodity stablecoin to trading depend on "all of the requirements in (4) or (5) as applicable". Paragraph (4) lists reserve criteria, but its test of reserve adequacy in (4)(c) speaks only of "reserves in respect of Fiat stablecoins". Paragraph (5) is not a criterion: it requires the operator to notify the AFSA within 3 business days after admission (in earlier versions, 10 days before admission). So for a Commodity stablecoin the operator has no stated test that the reserves cover the stablecoins in circulation. Issuers licensed in the AIFC must still meet the reserve rules in DAA 4.7.1, which cover Commodity stablecoins, and the AFSA approves stablecoins other than those issued by licensed Digital Asset Service Providers (2.8.1(3)(b)); the gap concerns the operator's admission test, mainly for stablecoins issued outside the AIFC. PMS 2.4.2(1)(c) has the same wording (AIFC2-PMS-02).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0151 — DAA 3.9.1(2) and 3.8.4(2): permission to combine items '(f) and (j)' copied from COB Schedule 3 after relettering
entry.summary: Reported. In COB Schedule 3 (source text) (f) is the price and (j) the firm's charges, so combining them gives an all-in price. DAA 3.9.1 drops COB item (c) (client's name), so the price is (e) and the charges (i); yet 3.9.1(2) still says '(f) and (j)' - now the execution-only statement and amounts received from another Person, which cannot form a single price. DAA 3.8.4 drops three COB items (principal/agent, client name, total payable) and ends at (i): '(j)' does not exist there at all (and the paragraph is numbered (2) without a (1)).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0150 — DAA 4.5(2): annual recovery/wind-down audit is attached to item (n), which became 'conflicts of interests'
entry.summary: Reported. DAA 4.5(2) requires an audit of "the policies and procedures required by DAA 4.5.1(n)". There is no rule 4.5.1; in 4.5(1) item (n) is now "conflicts of interests" and "recovery and winddown" is (o). In the version published as the initial version, (n) was "recovery and winddown". The letters changed in the consolidated version in force from 1 January 2025, and 4.5(2) was not updated. The subject of the audit ("the amount required to achieve recovery and orderly winddown") shows the intended item.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0149 — Part 4 covers issuers of Commodity stablecoins, but authorisation (4.1) and capital (4.2) name only Fiat stablecoins
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 3 (approved 13 April 2025, in force 13 October 2025) extended the Part 4 application statement to "issuing Fiat stablecoins and Commodity stablecoins", but in the same instrument added only "or issuing Fiat stablecoins" to 4.1(1), the lead-in of 4.2 and 4.2(b). The current version keeps this. Rule 4.11.3(1) says "In addition to DAA 4.2(b), an issuer of a Fiat stablecoin or Commodity stablecoin" must hold ongoing capital of 2%, so it assumes that 4.2(b) applies to both. GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 21, Guidance (5) also mentions only Fiat stablecoins. A Commodity-stablecoin issuer might be covered as "Providing Money Services in relation to Digital Assets" (buying and selling of a Digital Asset), but 4.1(2) treats issuing as a separate activity. The rules therefore do not say clearly which licence a Commodity-stablecoin issuer needs or whether the USD 200,000 floor in 4.2(b) applies to it.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0148 — Islamic banks — significant and non-significant investments: an investment that is significant under 4.29 through Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 instruments, with less than 10% of the common shares, is not covered by 4.43 or 4.45
entry.summary: Reported. IBB 4.29 defines a significant investment as an investment of 10% or more in the common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity concerned. Rule 4.43 applies where the Islamic Bank makes a non-significant investment and does not own 10% or more of the common shares; Rule 4.45 applies where it makes a significant investment and owns 10% or more of the common shares. An investment that is significant through Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 instruments, with less than 10% of the common shares, is outside both rules, and no other rule in 4.40 to 4.46 deducts it: 4.42 covers reciprocal cross holdings only, and 4.45(3) and 4.46 cover common shares and other CET 1 instruments only. The headings of 4.43 to 4.45 do not refer to the shareholding. Take an unconsolidated Islamic Bank whose only instrument other than common shares is an issue of Tier 2 sukuk of USD 300 million, with no reciprocal holding and no pledge: for an Islamic Bank with CET 1 Capital of USD 100 million, a holding of USD 30 million (10% of the issue) with no common shares is not deducted, while a holding of USD 29.7 million (9.9%) leads to a deduction of the excess of USD 19.7 million under 4.44.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0147 — Accumulated losses already reflected in retained earnings: IBB 4.13 and 4.39
entry.summary: Reported. IBB 4.13(c) includes retained earnings in Common Equity Tier 1 capital, and the Guidance to 4.13, which under IBB 1.3(b) is part of the rules, states that retained earnings and other comprehensive income include appropriated profit or loss. IBB 4.13(f) includes the regulatory adjustments under 4.30, which points to 4.31 to 4.45, and IBB 4.39 requires an Islamic Bank to deduct from its CET1 capital the amount of any accumulated losses, without distinguishing losses already reflected in retained earnings. Read as written, a loss of prior years reduces CET1 capital twice: an Islamic Bank with common shares of USD 100 million and retained earnings of minus USD 20 million would report CET1 of USD 60 million, or USD 80 million if 4.39 does not apply to losses already reflected in retained earnings. BBR 4.14(c) and 4.28(11) have the same structure, and BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 7 states the same for BBR 4.14.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0146 — NSFR required stable funding: unencumbered HQLA securities with a residual maturity of one year or more fall within the descriptions of two RSF categories
entry.summary: Reported. Under BPG Chapter 9 paragraph 177(a) each asset is assigned to one of the eight RSF categories, and BBR 9.19(2) requires the NSFR to be calculated in accordance with Chapter 9 of the BPG (it refers to Section E; the NSFR methodology is in Section H). Paragraph 179 assigns unencumbered Level 1 HQLA to Category 2 (5%), paragraphs 181 and 182(a) assign Level 2A and 2B HQLA to Categories 4 and 5 (15% and 50%), and paragraph 184(c) assigns 'unencumbered securities with residual maturity of 1 year or more' to Category 7 (85%). Unlike paragraph 184(d) and row 24 of the disclosure template Table 13, paragraph 184(c) does not exclude securities that qualify as HQLA, and no rule sets which description prevails. For a bank with available stable funding of USD 1,000 million, other required stable funding of USD 700 million and an unencumbered five-year Level 1 government bond of USD 500 million, the NSFR is 137.9% under paragraph 179 and 88.9% under paragraph 184(c). Form 201 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns repeats both lines (10.1 and 15.3), and IBB Appendix 1 paragraphs 131 and 136(c) repeat the same overlap (for an Islamic Bank, for example a Level 1 sovereign sukuk).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0145 — Maturity mismatch limits: the net cumulative position is inflows less outflows, and 9.21(4) requires it not to exceed negative 15% and negative 25%
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 9.21(1)(c) defines the net cumulative maturity mismatch position as inflows (assets) less outflows (liabilities) in each time band, and 9.21(3) expresses it as a percentage of Total Deposits; line 5 of Form 81 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns uses the same sign. Rule 9.21(4) then requires the position not to exceed negative 15% (sight to 8 days) and negative 25% (sight to 1 month), and the Bank must notify the AFSA if it exceeds these limits. Read as written, a bank with Total Deposits of USD 100 million whose inflows up to 8 days are USD 110 million and outflows USD 100 million (a position of +10%) exceeds negative 15% and breaches the limit, while a bank whose inflows are USD 40 million against outflows of USD 100 million (-60%) does not exceed it. The flows are those included in the maturity ladder under the BPG. IBB 10.30(4) and (5) have the same text (the denominator in IBB 10.30(3) also includes UPSIA accounts).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0144 — Significant and non-significant investments: the definition in 4.27, the heading of 4.29(4) and the conditions of 4.29(4)(a) and 4.29(6)(a) classify a holding of AT1 or T2 instruments differently
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 4.27 defines a significant investment as an investment of 10% or more in the common shares, or other instruments that qualify as capital, of the entity concerned. The heading of Rule 4.29(4), which is part of the Rules under section 24(1)(a) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts, describes non-significant investments as those "where the Bank does not own more than 10% of issued common equity of the entity". Rule 4.29(4) then applies where the Bank makes a non-significant investment and does not own more than 10% of the common shares, and Rule 4.29(6) where the Bank makes a significant investment and owns 10% or more of the common shares. A holding of 10% or more of an issue of AT1 or T2 instruments of another bank or insurer, with less than 10% of its common shares, is non-significant by the heading and significant by 4.27, and under the conditions of the two rules it is outside both of them. Take an unconsolidated issuer whose only instrument other than common shares is a T2 issue of USD 300 million, with no reciprocal holding and no pledge: for a bank with CET1 of USD 100 million, a holding of USD 30 million (10% of the issue) with no common shares is not deducted under the conditions of 4.29, while the heading and line 37 of Form 30 lead to a deduction of the excess of USD 20 million; a holding of USD 29.7 million (9.9%) leads to a deduction of USD 19.7 million. The heading also uses "not more than 10%" where 4.27 uses "10% or more".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0143 — Capital conservation ratios: Table 4A is entered by the CET1 capital ratio, while the buffer under 4.31(2) excludes CET1 used for the T1 and Total Capital ratios
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 4.31(2) provides that the capital conservation buffer must be made up of CET1 capital above the amounts used to meet the CET1, T1 and Total Capital ratios, and 4.32(1) requires a bank whose buffer falls below the required minimum to restrict its distributions. Under 4.32(2) and Table 4A, however, the minimum capital conservation ratio is selected by the bank's CET1 capital ratio, which does not exclude the CET1 used to meet the T1 and Total Capital ratios; a ratio above 7% gives 0%. For a bank whose capital is all CET1, the buffer becomes positive only above 8% of risk-weighted assets and reaches 2.5% at 10.5%. With risk-weighted assets of USD 1,000 million, CET1 of USD 85 million (8.5%) and no AT1 or T2 capital, the bank's ratios are above the minima, its buffer under 4.31(2) is USD 5 million against USD 25 million, so it is in breach of 4.31(1) and 4.32(1) requires it to restrict distributions; yet Table 4A sets no positive minimum retention (0%). BPG Chapter 4 paragraph 11(c) states that a bank with a CET1 capital ratio of more than 7% can distribute 100% of its earnings; 4.33(1) also compares CET1 with the CET1 ratio plus the buffer. IBB 5.2 to 5.4 and Table 5.1 have the same structure. Basel III paragraph 131 measures the CET1 ratio of the table excluding the CET1 needed for the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total Capital requirements.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0142 — "Insurance Manager" (an addressee of PRU(INT)) has no definition; PRU(INT) 1.3(2) uses "Insurance Mediation" instead of the GEN activity "Insurance Intermediation"
entry.summary: Reported. PRU(INT) 1.3(1) applies the rules to "Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers". The Glossary defines Insurance Intermediary but has no entry for Insurance Manager, and GEN defines the activity "Insurance Management" (Schedule 1, paragraph 24) but not the term "Insurance Manager". The addressee can be identified as a firm licensed for Insurance Management, but no text says so; the AFSA's Guidance to the AIFC Captive Insurance Regime states that "Insurance Manager is defined in the AIFC General Rules". Separately, 1.3(2) speaks of "an Authorisation to carry on Insurance Mediation"; the Regulated Activity is "Insurance Intermediation" (GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 15).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0141 — PRU(INT) 4.2(1): duty to vet the PI insurer is placed on 'the Insurance Intermediary' only, though the rule starts with 'an Authorised Firm'
entry.summary: Reported. PRU(INT) 4.2(1) reads: "Before an Authorised Firm takes out or renews a professional indemnity insurance policy with an insurer, the Insurance Intermediary must be satisfied ... that the insurer is a suitable Person to provide the insurance policy to the Insurance Intermediary". Under 1.3(1) "Authorised Firm" is used where rules apply to both Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers. Read with the opening words, 4.2(2)-(3) and 1.3(1), the duty probably covers Insurance Managers too, but the text names only the Insurance Intermediary. In the release of 10 December 2017 the whole sentence referred to the Insurance Intermediary; the amendments as of 2 December 2018 changed only the opening words.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0140 — PRU(INT) auditor certification covers quarterly returns submitted 'by the PRU Investment Firm' (copied from PRU INV)
entry.summary: Reported. PRU(INT) 5.2(2): the auditor's certification must relate to the annual returns and "each set of unaudited quarterly returns that have been submitted to the AFSA by the PRU Investment Firm in the previous year". A PRU Investment Firm is a category under the Prudential Rules for Investment Firms; PRU(INT) applies to Insurance Intermediaries and Insurance Managers, called together "Authorised Firm" (1.3(1)). 5.2(1) and the first sentence of 5.2(2) speak of an Authorised Firm, so the meaning survives. This is the converse of our observation AIFC-PRU-03, where PRU (Investment Firms) 3.2 refers to "the Insurance Intermediary".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0139 — TRR: Takaful Fund ring-fence exceptions refer to a non-existent "Rule 2.1.2 (1)", 2.2.3 to "rule 2.1.1", and 1.1.3(2) to 1.1.6(1) for the definition of Takaful Business
entry.summary: Reported. The prohibition on using Takaful Fund assets for other purposes is TRR 2.2.2(1), which itself announces "the exceptions provided for in the rest of this rule below"; the funds are established under 2.2.1. Yet 2.2.2(2), (3) and (4) say "Rule 2.1.2 (1) above does not ...", and 2.2.3 speaks of a Takaful Fund "established and maintained under rule 2.1.1". TRR 2.1 ("Overall Governance") has no numbered sub-rules. Separately, 1.1.3(2) refers to Takaful Business "as defined in Rules 1.1.6 (1)", but 1.1.6 lists principles and 1.1.5(1) defines a Takaful Operator; the activity of Takaful Business is defined in GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 25. The meaning survives in each case.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0138 — Notice to policyholders must include 'the Scheme Summary referred to in rule 11.8' - there is no rule 11.8 (PINS and TRR)
entry.summary: Reported. PINS 11.4.1(1)(b) and TRR 11.4.1(1)(b) refer to 'rule 11.8'; chapter 11 ends at 11.4.2. The Scheme Summary is defined in 11.2.3(a)(ii) and regulated in 11.3.3.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0137 — Glossary still defines 'Captive Insurer' as group-only, contrary to PINS 14.1.1 (Class 2 and 3 since 2020); FEES fee rows depend on it
entry.summary: Reported. Glossary V23: Captive Insurer = Licence to carry on Insurance Business 'only for the business or operations of the Group to which it belongs'. PINS 14.1.1-14.1.2 (since 13.12.2020): Class 2 may take up to 20% of GWP from third-party risks; Class 3 insures persons in similar businesses (group captives). The PINS 'Working Schedule 1' list of defined terms also keeps the group-only text. FEES V18 charges 'Captive Insurance Business' USD 7,000 (application) / 4,200 (annual) versus 'Insurance Business' 14,000 / 9,800.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0136 — Captive PCR: PINS 14.4.3(1) exempts Class 1, 2 and 3 captives, while the AFSA Guidance (2020) says only Class 1 is exempt
entry.summary: Reported. PINS 14.4.3(1) says Class 1, 2 and 3 Captive Insurers "are not required to calculate" the Prescribed Capital Requirement; 14.4.3(2) says each Cell of a Protected Cell Company "must calculate" it. Read with the heading, (2) is the specific rule for PCC cells. The AFSA's Guidance to the AIFC Captive Insurance Regime (13 December 2020) says only pure captives (Class 1) are exempt, which differs from 14.4.3(1).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0135 — General insurers must seek MER advice from "its Approved Actuary"; it is unclear whether insurers not otherwise required to have one must appoint one (PINS and TRR)
entry.summary: Reported. PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 10 applies to General Insurance Business. Paragraph 10.2(2) requires an insurer to "seek advice from its Approved Actuary" about its maximum event retention if it issues policies without a maximum amount insured, insures risks in multiple lines of business or has a complex portfolio. Under PINS 2.2.2(2) an Approved Actuary is mandatory for a general insurer only in certain cases, and PINS 9.2 deals with insurers "not required to have an Approved Actuary". The text does not say whether paragraph 10.2(2) itself requires such an insurer to appoint one, or whether it may use the independent actuary described in PINS 9.2.3. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 10.2(2) is the same.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0134 — Relief from the asset risk charge for assets excluded from Eligible Capital "in accordance with the table B1": the phrase can be read two ways (PINS and TRR)
entry.summary: Reported. PINS Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4: an insurer "need not include an amount in the asset risk charge for any asset excluded from Eligible Capital in accordance with the table B1 in paragraph 4.1". Table B1 sets charges and excludes nothing from Eligible Capital; the exclusions are in Schedule 3, paragraph 5. If the words "in accordance with the table B1" go with "the asset risk charge", the relief covers assets excluded under Schedule 3, which is the evident purpose. If they go with "excluded", the relief covers no asset. TRR Schedule 5, paragraph 4.4 is the same.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0133 — Two 'Category 3' in long-term categories; general categories 1-2 exclude a non-existent 'Category 4 (Permanent Health)' (PINS and TRR)
entry.summary: Reported. PINS Schedule 2 numbers both "Linked long-term" and "Permanent health" as Long-Term Insurance Category 3; there is no Category 4. General Insurance Categories 1 (Accident) and 2 (Sickness) in Schedule 1 exclude "contracts falling within Long-Term Insurance Category 4 (Permanent Health)". The name in brackets identifies the intended category, so the meaning survives. TRR Schedules 1 and 2 repeat this (Family Takaful Category 3 twice; General Takaful Categories 1 and 2 exclude Family Takaful Category 4).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0132 — Counterparty grade table omits Fitch 'BBB' (Grade 4 lists only BBB+ and BBB-) in PINS and TRR
entry.summary: Reported. In Table A of PINS Schedule 5 (counterparty grades), Grade 4 lists Fitch "BBB+" and "BBB-" but not "BBB"; the S&P column lists all three. TRR Schedule 5 Table A is identical. The order of the table points to Grade 4.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0131 — IBB NSFR rule cites 'Section E of Appendix 1' (does not exist) and then 'Section B' in the same paragraph
entry.summary: Reported. IBB 10.28(2) first says that the NSFR methodology is "set out in Section E of Appendix 1 of the IBB Module", and then refers to "Section B of Appendix 1" for the ASF and RSF factors. Appendix 1 has only Sections A (LCR), B (NSFR) and C (Maturity Mismatch). The meaning survives through the second sentence.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0130 — BPG not updated: it says Credit Providers are not Banking Business firms and excludes them from the leverage ratio, which BBR 4.36 has applied to Providing Credit since December 2022
entry.summary: Reported. BPG paragraph 6 says: "Credit Providers as defined in BBR 1.7 are not included in Banking Business firms according to BBR 1.4." BBR 1.4(3) has said since 2018 that a Banking Business firm may be a Credit Provider, and BPG paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 themselves include Credit Providers. The BPG tables also exclude Credit Providers from Section 4F (Rules 4.36-4.37, leverage ratio). That matched BBR 4.36 until the version with amendments as of 9 December 2022, which applies Section 4F to firms licensed for "Accepting Deposits" or "Providing Credit". The BPG (28 January 2019) has not been updated. The BBR prevail, so the problem is misleading guidance.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0129 — Fallback signatories of prudential returns: 'Risk Manager' is called a Controlled Function, but in GEN it is a Designated Function
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 3.7(2) requires, if the primary signatories are unavailable, signature by 'both of the individuals approved to exercise the following Controlled Functions: (a) the Risk Manager function; (b) the Compliance Officer function'. GEN 2.2.1 lists Controlled Functions as GEN 2.2.2-2.2.5 (SEO, Director, Finance Officer, Compliance Officer); Risk Manager is GEN 2.3.5 and may be held by a Designated Individual who is not AFSA-approved (GEN 2.1.2(2)). In GEN at the BBR's adoption (2018) there was no Risk Manager function at all.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0128 — Operational risk policy rule copied from market risk: Governing Body must ensure a bank-wide view of 'Market Risk exposures'
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 7.1(5) repeats 6.1(4) word for word except for the name of the policy: the operational risk management policy must give "a comprehensive bank-wide view of its Market Risk exposures" and take into account "the risk of a significant deterioration in market liquidity of its exposures". BBR 7.1(4)(d) likewise ties the review of the operational risk policy to the "nature, scale and complexity of its Trading Book activities" (copied from 6.1(3)(d)). The substance is partly covered elsewhere: 7.5(1)(a) requires the bank to identify operational risks in all its products, activities, processes and systems, and 7.5(1)(f) requires reporting to the Governing Body.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0127 — AT1 and T2 definitions cite Rule 4.28 (CET1 adjustments); the CET1 definition cites only Rule 4.29
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 4.16(d) and 4.18(d) say AT1 and T2 capital are adjusted "in accordance with Rule 4.28", but 4.28 is "Adjustments to CET1 Capital". BBR 4.14(f) refers to Rule 4.29 for CET1; 4.29 does contain CET1 deductions, but the CET1 adjustments in 4.28 and 4.30 are not mentioned. The rules operate directly, so there is no practical effect.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0126 — Table 4A capital conservation ratios: rows share boundary values ('to' / '≥') and 7.0% sits between '≥6.375% to 7.0%' and '>7%'
entry.summary: Reported. BBR Table 4A uses the bands "4.5% to 5.125%", "≥5.125% to 5.75%", "≥5.75% to 6.375%", "≥6.375% to 7.0%" and ">7%". If "to" includes the upper value, 5.125%, 5.75% and 6.375% fall in two rows; if it excludes it, as the "≥" signs suggest, exactly 7.0% falls in no row (rule 4.32(1) then limits the restriction to a buffer below the minimum). At exactly 5.125% the table (row 2, 80% conservation) and the BPG Chapter 4 guidance, paragraph 11(a) ("less than or equal to 5.125%", 100%), give different results. IBB Table 5.1 uses "X% or more but less than Y%" and "≥7%".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0125 — Threshold deduction: 10% per item 'or' 15% aggregate; (4) deducts the excess over '(3)(a) or (b)' - outcome indeterminate
entry.summary: Reported. 4.30(3) grants full recognition (300%/400% risk weight, no deduction) 'provided that (a) each item is no more than 10% ...; or (b) in total, the 3 items are no more than 15%'. With 'or', a bank whose items are each under 10% but total over 15% satisfies (a) and needs no deduction, while 4.30(4) requires deduction of 'any amount in excess of the threshold in (3)(a) or (b)', which can be read as the excess over 15%. The same 'or' is in IBB 4.46(3). (Also '(net of all regulatory adjustments except those under this Subdivision)': there are no Subdivisions in BBR.) With three items of USD 9 million each and CET1 of USD 100 million, the text yields a deduction of 0 (sub-rule (3)(a)) and of USD 12 million (sub-rule (4) by reference to (3)(b)). A bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 800 million and a market risk requirement of USD 10 million then both meets and breaches its capital requirement under 4.9 (USD 100 million against 97.64 million; USD 88 million against 93.8 million). Lines 38-40 and 44 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns apply the 10% and 15% limits together.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0124 — Allocation of the 10% excess across tiers uses the bank's OWN capital as numerator and holdings as denominator; shares do not sum to 1
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 4.29(5)(c) allocates the excess over 10% to each tier of capital by the formula Excess x A/B, where A is "the amount of CET 1 capital, additional tier 1 capital or tier 2 capital of the Bank" and B is "the total capital holdings of the Bank". Read literally, A is the bank's own capital in a tier, while B is its holdings in other entities, so the three shares do not add up to 1. For example, with own CET1, AT1 and T2 of 100, 10 and 20, holdings of 12 (CET1) and 3 (T2) and an excess of 5, the literal formula deducts 43.3 in total instead of 5. Under 4.29(1)(b) deductions are made from the tier for which the held capital would qualify, which points to A being the bank's holdings in that tier. "Capital holdings" is not defined. IBB 4.44(3) has the same wording. With holdings of USD 15 million, all in CET1 instruments, and own CET1 of USD 100 million, the literal formula deducts USD 33.3 million instead of 5 million; with holdings of USD 150 million it deducts USD 93.3 million instead of 140 million. For a bank with other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 900 million, a market risk requirement of USD 10 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 15 million (capital requirement USD 99.4 million), Total Capital after the allocation is USD 86.7 million under the literal formula and USD 125 million if A is the holdings of each tier.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0123 — Securitisation exposures: Table 5C row 10 or Table 5H? No rule says which applies to an originator's or sponsor's retained positions
entry.summary: Reported. BBR has two risk-weight tables for securitisation exposures. Table 5B item 9 sends "claims on securitisation exposures" to Table 5C row 10 (50% to 250%; unrated 150%). Rule 5.21(16) applies Table 5H (20% to 350%; B+ and below or unrated 1,250% or deduction) to on-balance-sheet retained securitisation exposures, which 5.21(12)-(13) link to a Bank that is an originator or sponsor, including its investments in the securitisation. Read as a specific rule, 5.21(16) governs those positions and Table 5C row 10 the positions of other investors. But no rule says so, and 5.21(7) speaks of applying Table 5H to "a securitisation exposure" in general. The weights differ widely, for example 50% against 20% for AAA and 150% against 1,250% for an unrated exposure.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0122 — BBR cites BPG Chapter 9 Sections D, E and F for the LCR, NSFR and maturity mismatch; in the BPG these are Sections G, H and I
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 9.16(5)(b) (the AFSA's power to adjust "requirements under section D of Chapter 9 of the BPG" for HQLA and net cash outflows), 9.19(2) (NSFR methodology, "Section E", twice) and 9.21(1)(a) (maturity-ladder methodology, "section F") cite BPG Chapter 9 by section letter; the notes to 9.16(3) and 9.21 do the same. In the published BPG (AFSA-L-GB-2019-0001, 28 January 2019) Sections D, E and F of Chapter 9 are Funding Strategy, Stress Testing and Contingency Funding Plan; the LCR, NSFR and Maturity Mismatch Approach are Sections G, H and I. The right sections can be found by their titles.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0121 — LCR powers: appeal and procedure refer to '(4)(a)-(e)' and '(1)(d)' instead of 9.16(5)
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 9.16(5)(a)-(e) lists the AFSA's powers on the liquidity coverage ratio. Sub-rules (6), (7) and (8) refer to "(4)(a), (b), (c) or (e)" and "(1)(d)", but 9.16(4) and 9.16(1) have no such paragraphs. The sister rule IBB 10.25(6)-(8) cites (5). The Framework Regulations still give procedure and appeal rights, so the meaning survives.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0120 — Basic indicator approach: GI is defined as an average, and the formula divides it by n again
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 7.6(2) sets the operational risk capital requirement as GI x alpha / n. GI is defined as "the Bank's average annual gross income" for the years (out of the previous 3) in which it is positive, and n is the number of those years. The average is therefore divided by n a second time, and the result falls as the number of positive years grows: with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years the requirement is 50 x 15% / 3 = USD 2.5 million; with USD 50 million in one year and losses in the other two it is USD 7.5 million. Sub-rule (3) speaks of excluding loss years "from both the numerator and denominator when calculating the average". The difference concerns the operational risk component, which enters risk-weighted assets at 12.5 times the requirement (BBR 4.7(2)(b)), not the whole capital requirement. IBB 9.10(2) has the same formula and definition. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with gross income of USD 50 million in each of three years, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and Total Capital of USD 45 million, the requirement under 4.9 is USD 42.5 million as printed and USD 47.5 million if gross income is averaged once, so the bank meets or breaches the 8% Total Capital ratio depending on the reading (8.47% against 7.58%). The AFSA return (Annex 1.13 of the Manual for Preparation of Returns) computes a single "Average GI" over the positive years and does not divide it by n again.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0119 — Non-significant investments: holdings below 10% of CET1 are deducted in full, holdings at or above 10% only above the threshold
entry.summary: Reported. BBR 4.29(4) applies when, after other regulatory adjustments, the total of the deductions under that rule is less than 10% of the Bank's CET1 capital; the Bank must then deduct the investments in full (4.29(4)(b)-(c)). BBR 4.29(5) applies when the total is 10% or more and deducts only the amount by which it exceeds 10% (the excess). With CET1 of 100, holdings of 9.9 are deducted in full (9.9), holdings of 10 lead to no deduction and holdings of 11 to a deduction of 1. A bank can therefore keep more CET1 by holding more. IBB 4.43 and 4.44 have the same structure. Carried through to the capital ratios: for a bank with CET1 of USD 50 million, other credit risk-weighted assets of USD 450 million, a market risk requirement of USD 4 million and an operational risk requirement of USD 7.5 million, holdings of USD 4.9 million are deducted in full and the bank falls below its capital requirement under 4.9 and the 8% Total Capital ratio (USD 45.1 million against 47.5 million); holdings of USD 5.0 million are not deducted and the bank meets them (USD 50 million against 48.7 million). Line 37 of Form 30 in the Manual for Preparation of Returns deducts only the amount above the 10% threshold.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0118 — IFR 7.3 requires SSB approval of a Fund's "Prospectus", a Glossary term for securities prospectuses; Funds issue "Offering Materials"
entry.summary: Reported. IFR 7.3(1) and (2) require a Fund’s Constitution "and Prospectus" to be approved by an SSB and reviewed every year; the Guidance under 7.2 also speaks of the Fund’s "most recent Prospectus". In the Glossary, "Prospectus" is the document referred to in MAR 1.3, which an unlisted Fund does not issue; such a Fund gives investors "Offering Materials" (CIS 5.3), and IFR itself uses that term in 7.8. Read with 7.8, "Prospectus" in 7.3 can be understood as the Fund’s Offering Materials, but the defined term points elsewhere. CIS has moved to the same term for Funds: Amendments No. 7 to CIS (in force 1 January 2025) replaced "Prospectus" with "Offering Materials" in the Feeder Fund rules. IFR 7.3 was not aligned.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0117 — IFR 7.5(3) and the draft Shari'ah Governance Rules: does a Fund that relies on Shari'ah screening keep its relief from appointing an SSB?
entry.summary: Reported. Under the current IFR, 7.5(3) releases the Fund Manager of a Non-Exempt Fund from appointing an SSB where it relies on a widely accepted Shari'ah screening process, while 7.3(1), 7.6(2) and 7.7(1) refer to "the Fund's SSB" without an exception. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0003 deletes IFR 7.5 to 7.7 and places Shari'ah governance in new Shari'ah Governance Rules, which apply to "a Fund Manager of a Domestic Fund which is operated or held out as being operated as an Islamic Fund" (rule 1(1)(b)). After adoption the conflict inside IFR falls away with 7.5 to 7.7. Two questions remain: the new Rules contain no counterpart of the screening relief in 7.5(3), so it is unclear whether such Funds must now appoint an SSB; and IFR 7.3(1), which the draft does not amend, still requires approval by "the Fund's SSB".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0116 — AFSA online CIS misses other Amendments No. 7 changes: Venture Capital Fund (2.4(b)(iii)), 7.6(b) "Associates", and rule 1.6 without text
entry.summary: Reported. The AFSA online CIS includes many changes made by Amendments No. 7 (in force 1 January 2025), but not these: (1) 2.4(b)(iii) still describes a Venture Capital Fund as "an Exempt Fund and a Domestic Fund" that invests "in the equity share capital" of unlisted businesses; Amendments No. 7 deleted "and a Domestic Fund" and replaced "equity share capital" with "Securities and Units", while the online text already shows the feeder route added by the same amendment; (2) 7.6(b) still says "Associates" where Amendments No. 7 put "Related Parties"; (3) rule 1.6 (when a Fund invests in Digital Assets indirectly), inserted by Amendments No. 7, has a heading but no text under it.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0115 — AFSA online CIS shows rule 10.1 in the 2018 wording, without Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers added by Amendments No. 2 (2019)
entry.summary: Reported. The AFSA online CIS still shows 10.1 in the 2018 wording: "This chapter applies to all Funds managed by Fund Managers located in the AIFC." Since Amendments No. 2 (2019), 10.1 also covers (b) Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers. The online text therefore leaves those Funds outside 10.2, 10.3 and 10.6.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0114 — AFSA online CIS Schedule 2(a)(i) still reads "Non-Compliant Country"; Amendments No. 7 deleted "Non-" from 1 January 2025
entry.summary: Reported. CIS Schedule 2(a)(i) lists, as a criterion for a Recognised Jurisdiction, that "the jurisdiction is listed as a Compliant Country or Territory by the Financial Action Task Force" (V8). Amendments No. 7 (approved 15 December 2024, in force 1 January 2025) deleted the word "Non-" from this item; the amending instrument shows it as struck through. The AFSA online CIS still reads "Non-Compliant Country or Territory" and shows no deleted (struck-through) text at that place. Versions V3 to V7 of the act carried the word "Non-" from 2019 to the end of 2024; Amendments No. 7 fixed the act, but not the online text.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0113 — "Single Family Office Fund" and "Corporate Treasury Centre Fund" are not defined, and the CTC Fund is spelled three ways
entry.summary: Reported. CIS gives relief to Single Family Office Funds and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds (7.2-1.2, 7.2-1.3, 4.2(d)(i), 6.2(a)), but the two terms are not defined in CIS or the Glossary. A third spelling, "Corporate Treasury Fund", appears in 5.3(b) and the heading of 10.5-1.1. The classes can largely be identified from the defined terms "Single Family Office" and "Corporate Treasury Centre" and from 7.2-1.2, 7.2-1.3, 6.14 and 10.5-1(j), so the gap is one of definition and spelling.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0112 — Reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds: the draft extends CIS 10.4 and 10.5 to every Domestic Fund, but 10.5(b) and the Guidance to 2.4.17 do not match
entry.summary: Reported. Under the current CIS, reports on Single Family Office and Corporate Treasury Centre Funds (10.5-1(j), 10.5-1.1) have no deadline, frequency or recipient: both Funds must be Exempt Funds, and 10.5, which sets the timing and recipients of Fund reports, applies to Non-Exempt Funds only (10.1(ii)). CIS also does not require these Funds to be audited (10.4 and 10.1(i)). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 extends the audit rule in 10.4 and the periodic reports in 10.5(a) to each Domestic Fund, which answers most of this point. Two questions remain on the draft. First, 10.5(b) still sets the four-month deadline for the annual report "for the Non-Exempt Fund", while 10.5(c) no longer says "Non-Exempt", so the deadline for the annual report of other Domestic Funds is unclear. Second, the Guidance to the new 2.4.17 says that for a Corporate Treasury Centre Fund "the standard Fund Manager reporting requirements under CIS 10.5 also do not apply", while the draft 10.5(a) covers each Domestic Fund and states no exception.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0111 — CIS 7.7: 'Related Person Transaction' covers 'any other Fund managed by the Fund', not by the Fund Manager as the heading says
entry.summary: Reported. CIS 7.7(a) and (d) refer to "any other Fund managed by the Fund or any of its Associates". A Fund does not manage other Funds; the heading of 7.7 speaks of Funds "managed by the Fund Manager". The meaning survives through the heading and the Associate limb, but the wording has no referent.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0110 — Custody for domestic Exempt Funds: CIS 7.3(d) requires an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2", but chapter 8 applies only to other Funds; do its exceptions apply?
entry.summary: Reported. CIS chapter 7 applies to Domestic Fund Managers "in respect of all Funds" (7.1), so 7.3(d) — delegate custody to an Eligible Custodian "in accordance with Rule 8.2" — reaches domestic Exempt Funds. Chapter 8, including the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e), applies only to Non-Exempt Funds and REITs of Domestic Fund Managers and to Exempt Funds of Foreign Fund Managers (8.1). The words "in accordance with Rule 8.2" can be read to bring the exceptions in 8.2(b) and (e) with them, and the general waiver in CIS 1.3 is also available, but the text does not say so. Separately, PRU(INV) Table 3.3 assumes that a Single Family Office Fund does not need an Eligible Custodian; CIS has no such rule. This overlaps with our earlier item on PRU(INV) Table 3.3 (AIFC-PRU-01).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0109 — CIS 5.1 disapplies 5.3(b)(i) (investment objective, strategy, leverage) for Non-Exempt Funds; in the draft, 5.1 refers to the deleted rule 5.3
entry.summary: Reported. CIS 5.1(a) applies 5.3 to all Funds "excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j)", and 5.1(b) applies "5.3(b)(i) and (j)" to Exempt Funds only. 5.3(b)(i) is the core disclosure of the investment objective, policy and strategy, asset types, risks and leverage, including the maximum level of leverage. The items that are Exempt-only by nature are 5.3(i) (the Exempt Fund legend) and 5.3(j) (the legend for an Exempt Fund of a Foreign Fund Manager). Read literally, a Non-Exempt (retail) Fund is relieved of 5.3(b)(i) while Exempt Funds must give it. The opening words of 5.3(b) and Schedule 1(j) still bind every Fund, so what is literally lost is the specific list, including the maximum level of leverage. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes rule 5.3 and moves its content to the new 5.4, 5.5 and Schedule 1-1, while 5.1(a) and (b) still refer to "5.3 (excluding 5.3(b)(i) and (j))" and "5.3(b)(i) and (j)". If the draft is adopted as published, both references will point to a deleted rule.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0108 — CIS 5.3(l)(ii) refers to 'property related assets, referred to in 3.1(b)' — CIS 3.1 has no paragraph (b)
entry.summary: Reported. 5.3(l)(ii) requires disclosure of the percentage of net assets that may consist of 'property related assets, referred to in 3.1(b)'. CIS 3.1 is the one-paragraph 'Application' rule of chapter 3 (arrangements not amounting to a CIS) and has no (b); no other rulebook is named. 'Property related assets' is not defined in CIS or Glossary V23.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0107 — CIS 5.3(l) is headed 'Information relating to a Feeder Fund' but sets property-fund disclosures; 'Property Fund' is not defined
entry.summary: Reported. Paragraph (l) of CIS 5.3 opens 'Information relating to a Feeder Fund:' and then lists only real-estate items: investment in Real Property, the 'Property Fund's' net assets in property-related assets, vacant or mortgaged properties, valuer under 6.10(b), insurance of Real Property, single-property funds, REIT vehicle. Nothing in (l) concerns Feeder Funds (whose disclosures sit in 2.4-1(c)(v)). The term 'Property Fund' used in (l)(ii), (iv), (v), (vi)(E), (vii) and Schedule 1 (j)(i) is not defined in CIS or in Glossary V23. Under s.24 of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts the heading is part of the act, so the text names one scope (Feeder Funds) and the content implies another (funds investing in Real Property, incl. REITs).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0106 — Disclosure item for a Fund Manager acting itself as custodian of Real Property points to CIS 7.3(e), which the same amending instrument deleted
entry.summary: Reported. CIS 5.3(l)(viii) requires three disclosures "If the Fund Manager itself acts as the custodian of Real Property, in accordance with CIS 7.3.(e)". CIS 7.3(e) reads "[intentionally omitted]": Amendments No. 3 (in force 1 June 2023) inserted 5.3(l)(viii) with this reference and, on the same page, deleted the whole of 7.3(e), which was the custody exemption for a Self-managed Fund. The reference therefore has no target. A Fund may still have no Eligible Custodian under 8.2(b), or under a waiver (8.2(e) or 1.3), but CIS does not describe any of these cases as the Fund Manager itself acting as custodian, so it is unclear when the disclosure applies. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 deletes the words "Subject to Rule (e), and" in 7.3(d) but moves the disclosure item, with the same reference to 7.3(e), into the new CIS 5.6.2(h).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0105 — COB 1.2.2(c) applies COB 8 (Client Assets) to Authorised Crowdfunding Platforms, but the reading rule does not reach the scope of COB 8, which is defined by Investment Business
entry.summary: Reported. COB 1.2.2(c) disapplies COB for an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform except COB 3, COB 4, COB 7, "COB 8 (Client Assets)" and COB Schedule 2, and the reading rule that follows provides that in these chapters "Regulated Activities" shall be read as "Market Activities". COB 8 does not use that term to set its scope: it applies to a firm that holds Money for a Client "in the course of, or in connection with, the carrying on of Investment Business or Provides Money Services" (COB 8.1.2(a), 8.1.4), and COB 8.2.1 defines Client Money by Investment Business. Operating a Loan or Investment Crowdfunding Platform is a Market Activity and is not in the Glossary definition of Investment Business. Read literally, the Client Money Rules do not attach to money a platform holds for lenders or investors, for example before the target funding amount is reached (AMI 7.3.22) or when it collects repayments for lenders (AMI 7.4.2), unless the platform also holds a licence for Investment Business or Money Services (AMI 7.2.1). AMI 2.9.1 requires satisfactory arrangements for safeguarding users' assets, and AMI 7.3.4(1)(n) requires disclosure of the "arrangements and safeguards for Client Assets held or controlled by an Authorised Crowdfunding Platform", but these rules do not set out the client money rules or the distribution rules in COB 8.2.16. Example: lenders transfer 900,000 USD to a platform for a loan with a target of 1,000,000 USD; the platform fails before the target is reached; whether the 900,000 USD is Client Money protected by COB 8.2.16 depends on whether COB 8 is read as reaching Market Activities.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0104 — AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 (Amendments No. 7, 29 June 2022)
entry.summary: Reported. The AFSA online Market Rules do not contain MAR 1.9.3 (Expert’s responsibility) and 1.9.4 (Exceptions from liability), which Amendments No. 7 inserted with effect from 29 June 2022. In the online text, 1.9.2 (Limitations on the application of MAR 1.9.1) is followed directly by 1.10 (AIFC ESG Debentures). The consolidated versions V8 to V13 on aifc.kz contain both rules. The online text applied another change made by the same instrument (MAR 2.1(2), which excludes Listed Funds and Exempt Offerors from MAR 2), but not its change to MAR 3.1-1(1), which in the act also excludes an Exempt Offeror from MAR 3. The online Schedule 4, paragraph 1(a)(ii) still refers to "consent under MAR 1.9.3", and the Glossary defines "Expert" by MAR 1.9.3; a reader of the online rulebook cannot find that rule. Our earlier observation on the Glossary entry "Expert" (AIFC-GLO-06) relied on the online text and is withdrawn: the definition resolves in the act. MAR 1.9.4(4)(a) has a separate wrong reference (see AIFC2-MKT-05).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0103 — REC 1.1.4(a): should the comparison also cover Chapter 2 of Part 3 of the Framework Regulations?
entry.summary: Reported. REC 1.1.4 is made for section 89(3)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which asks whether investors get protection equivalent to the requirements for licensing an Authorised Market Institution "in Chapter 2 of Part 3". REC 1.1.4(a) asks the applicant to compare its home rules "with Part 4 of the Framework Regulations and Chapters 2 and 3 or 4 (as appropriate) of the AMI Rules". Part 4 is "Controlled and Designated Functions". The AMI chapters cover much of what section 89(3)(a) protects, and controlled functions are also relevant, but Chapter 2 of Part 3 is not named.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0102 — MOTF 8.1(2)-(3), 6.3 and 20.1: cross-references garbled ('8.1((a)a(a)', '8.1(a)(i)(i)(a)(i)(i)', '6.2(a)(i)', '20.1(1)(1)')
entry.summary: Reported. MOTF 8.1(1) has paragraphs (a) to (c). 8.1(2) says "For the purposes of MOTF 8.1((a)a(a)"; 8.1(3)(a) "MOTF 8.1(a)a(b)"; 8.1(3)(b) "MOTF 8.1(a)(i)(i)(a)(i)(i)"; 8.1(3)(c) "MOTF 8.1(a)(i)(i)(1)". MOTF 6.2 has items (i) and (ii) without (a), yet 6.3 waives "MOTF 6.2(a)(i)". MOTF 20.1(1) has no sub-paragraph, yet 20.1(2) to (4) refer to "MOTF 20.1(1)(1)". The AFSA online text is the same. For 8.1(2) and 6.3 the target follows from the content (8.1(1)(a), error checking; 6.2(i), public consultation). For 8.1(3)(a) it is unclear whether "made public" qualifies 8.1(1)(b) (consolidation of data) or (c) (availability to the public).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0101 — 'Environmental Instrument Tokens' (AMI 2.6.1(3)) is undefined; the Glossary instead has a second 'Commodity Derivative Token' entry in the E-position
entry.summary: Reported. AMI 2.6.1(3) requires a direct-access Member whose access is only for "Commodity Derivative Tokens or Environmental Instrument Tokens" to be a Professional Client. "Environmental Instrument Token" is not defined in the Glossary. Glossary V23 has two entries "Commodity Derivative Token" with the same text: one in alphabetical place under C, and a second one directly after "Environmental Instrument". The AFSA online Glossary has the same duplicate. The second entry may have been meant to define "Environmental Instrument Token"; the text does not show this.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0100 — AMI 2-1.2.2(4) refers to the annual audit 'required under AMI 2-1.5'; AMI has no 2-1.5 (audit is 2-1.4)
entry.summary: Reported. AMI 2-1.2.2(4) requires systems and controls embedded in DLT to be "included within the scope of the annual audit and written report required under AMI 2-1.5". Chapter 2-1 (in AMI since V8, 1 January 2024) ends with 2-1.4 "Technology audit reports", which contains the annual audit and written report. In V8 to V11 there is no AMI 2-1.5.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0099 — MAR Schedule 4 para 4(a)(iii) points to 'technology and governance requirements set out in AMI 2-1.2'; those are in AMI 2-1.1
entry.summary: Reported. MAR Schedule 4 para 4(a)(iii) requires a Security Token prospectus to explain 'how the operator of the facility meets the technology and governance requirements set out in AMI 2-1.2'. In AMI V11 the technology and governance requirements are AMI 2-1.1 ('Technology and governance requirements'); AMI 2-1.2 is 'Operating a facility for Investment Tokens that permits direct access'. The same mismatch existed when Schedule 4 was introduced (AMI V8, 1 Jan 2024).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0098 — MAR 2.4.5(b) refers to "a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules": which Takeover Rules apply?
entry.summary: Reported. MAR 2.4.5(b) lifts the closed-period dealing ban for "undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a Takeover Offer under the Takeover Rules". The Glossary defines "Takeover Rules" as Rules prescribed by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a) of the Framework Regulations, which says that the AFSA "may prescribe" such Rules. We did not find any Takeover Rules among the acts published on aifc.kz or in the AFSA online rulebook. Chapter 11 of Part 7 of the AIFC Companies Regulations ("Protection of Minorities in Takeovers") is part of the Regulations, not Rules made by the AFSA under section 88(1)(a). If no Takeover Rules have been made, exemption (b) has nothing to apply to, and a Restricted Person would need clearance under MAR 2.4.4.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0097 — MAR 5.5.3: the closing words "prior to conducting a Market Sounding" also cover the record of disclosures in (c), which can only be completed after the sounding
entry.summary: Reported. MAR 5.5.3 lists four steps (a) to (d) and then, on a separate line after (d), the words "prior to conducting a Market Sounding". Laid out this way, the words govern the whole list. Steps (a) and (b) already carry their own timing. Step (c) requires a record of the disclosures, including "the date and time of each disclosure", which cannot be complete before the sounding. The AFSA online text joins the closing words to (d) instead. The second sentence of (c) also asks for the record to be given to "the competent authority", while (d) names the AFSA.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0096 — MAR 1.9.4(4)(a): the Expert limb of the correction defence refers to "(2)(c)", which is not about Expert statements; the Expert paragraph is (3)
entry.summary: Reported. MAR 1.9.4(4)(a) gives a defence where, before acquisition, "a correction or, where the statement was such as is mentioned in (2)(c), the fact that the Expert was not competent or had not consented" was published. Paragraph (2)(c) is the general correction defence and describes no statement; statements made on the authority of an Expert are dealt with in (3). Read literally, the second limb of (4)(a) has no case to apply to. The same reference is already in Amendments No. 7 (29 June 2022), which inserted 1.9.3 and 1.9.4: the instrument lettered the top-level paragraphs (a) to (f) but its own cross-references already used the numbers (2) to (6), so "(2)(c)" pointed to the correction defence from the start. The DFSA and ADGM market rules from which this text comes have the same reference (DFSA MKT 2.11.1(4)(a), ADGM MKT 4.11.1(4)(a)). MAR 1.9.3 and 1.9.4 appear in the consolidated MAR (V13) on aifc.kz but not in the AFSA online rulebook (see AIFC2-MKT-13).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0095 — MAR 6.2.2 heading refers to 'MAR 8.2.2 (Obligation to draw up insider lists)'; MAR has no chapter 8
entry.summary: Reported. The heading of MAR 6.2.2 reads 'Reporting Entity is responsible for complying with MAR 8.2.2 (Obligation to draw up insider lists)'. MAR ends with chapter 7 and Schedules 1-4; the obligation to draw up insider lists is MAR 6.2.1. The number has been wrong since the initial version (2017) and is repeated in the table of contents and on the regulator's site.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0094 — MAR 5.5.2, 6.1.7, 6.2.2 and 6.4.3: references printed as "MAR 5.2.65", "MAR 6.2.21" and "MAR 5.2.6.6" name no existing rule
entry.summary: Reported. Four references in the market abuse and disclosure chapters name rules that do not exist: "MAR 5.2.65" (5.5.2 and 6.1.7), "MAR 6.2.21" (6.2.2) and "MAR 5.2.6.6" (6.4.3). Up to V4 (14 February 2019) these places read "MAR 5.2.6" and "MAR 6.2.2"; the merged numbers first appear in V5 (2019), and we found no amending instrument that made that change. Amendments No. 6 (2020) shows "5.2.5" as new text in 6.1.7, next to a broken field code ("Error! Reference source not found."), and its text of 6.2.2 and 6.4.3 is also damaged; V7 to V13 still print "MAR 5.2.65". The AFSA online text is the same. The bracketed titles show the intended targets for three of the places: 5.2.5 (Unlawful disclosure of Inside Information) in 5.5.2 and 6.1.7, and 6.2.1 (Obligation to draw up insider lists) in 6.2.2. In 6.4.3 there is no title.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0093 — MAR 5.2.2(a) in the consolidated PDFs V9–V13 on aifc.kz still refers to itself; Amendments No. 8 changed it to MAR 5.2.1
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 8 to the Market Rules (approved 25 June 2023, in force 1 August 2023) replaced "5.2.2" with "5.2.1" in MAR 5.2.2(a) and added the closing bracket. The consolidated versions V9 (1 August 2023) to V13 (1 January 2026) published on aifc.kz applied the other edits in the same line ("of", "Investments") but still read "has the meaning given in MAR 5.2.2 (Definition of Inside Information (general); and", so the definition refers to itself. The AFSA online rulebook already reads "MAR 5.2.1". The bracketed title points to 5.2.1, so the meaning survives.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0092 — MAR 1.1.2(1)(b): is an offer that meets both (2)(c) and (2)(d) meant to lose the placement exemption?
entry.summary: Reported. MAR 1.1.2(1)(b) exempts an offer by way of placement only if it satisfies "one and one only" of the conditions in (2); (1)(c) allows combinations only where one of them is (a), (b) or (m). An offer of Securities denominated in units of at least USD 100,000 (condition (d)) and issued at or above that amount also meets condition (c), because every investor pays at least USD 100,000. Read literally, such an offer is not exempt unless it also meets (a), (b) or (m), while the same offer issued below USD 100,000 per unit would be. For Exempt Securities, MAR 1.2.2(1) uses "one or more of the conditions". The words "one and one only" may be meant to stop the stacking of exemptions, but the text does not say which combinations are excluded.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0091 — COB 8.5.13(2) and the 16.2 table use the undefined 'Insurance Bank Account'
entry.summary: Reported. COB 8.5 requires Client Money to be held in "Client Money Accounts" (8.5.6, 8.5.9). COB 8.5.13(2) requires records of "all sums withdrawn from the Insurance Bank Account as a result of credit taken under COB 8.5.12", and the table in COB 16.2 repeats it. "Insurance Bank Account" is not defined in COB or in the Glossary and is used nowhere else. The term has been in COB since the first version (then COB 11.8.12). The meaning (the Client Money Account) can be recovered from 8.5.9 and 8.5.12.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0090 — Client asset rules give regulatory roles to 'the AIFC' (the Centre) where the regulator, the AFSA, is meant
entry.summary: Reported. The Glossary defines AIFC as the Astana International Financial Centre (a territory/regime). COB nevertheless says: firms must demonstrate grounds 'to the AIFC's satisfaction' (8.2.11, 8.3.8); Client Money may be paid out in circumstances 'otherwise authorised by the AIFC' (8.2.13(e)); disclosure of 'other Distribution Event stipulated by the AIFC' (8.2.18(a)(ii)). The parallel collateral disclosure (8.3.2(d)) says 'stipulated by the AFSA', and the Glossary Distribution Event (c) is a direction by the AFSA.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0089 — COB 5.6.11 names Insurance Intermediaries for the Takaful disclosure, but COB 1.2.3 does not list it among the rules that apply to them
entry.summary: Reported. COB 1.2.3 says that COB does not apply to Insurance Intermediaries "with the exception of COB 3, COB 4, COB 8.5 and COB 11". COB 5.6.11(1), inserted with the Takaful amendments in 2018, names "an Insurance Intermediary" among the persons who must explain the differences between Takaful and conventional contracts. When COB 8.5 was added to the list in 1.2.3, 5.6.11 was not. Because 5.6.11 names Insurance Intermediaries expressly, it is best read as applying to them, but 1.2.3 does not say so.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0088 — COB 6.1.1(a) keeps COB 6.2.9 for Market Counterparty transactions, but COB 6.2.1(a) disapplies all of COB 6.2 for them
entry.summary: Reported. COB 6.1.1(a): COB 6 does not apply to a transaction 'it undertakes with a Market Counterparty, except for COB 6.2.9'. The table in 1.2.7 repeats the exception. COB 6.2.1(a): 'The Rules in COB 6.2 do not apply ... to any transaction which: (a) it undertakes with a Market Counterparty' - with no exception, and 6.2.9 is inside 6.2.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0087 — Amendments No. 14 apply COB 8.2 to Money Service Providers but 'Client Money' (8.2.1, Glossary) still covers only Investment Business money
entry.summary: Reported. Since Amendments No. 14 (13 January 2026), COB 8.1.2 and 8.1.4 require an Authorised Firm that Provides Money Services to comply with COB 8.2, and PMS 9.1 sends a Money Service Provider to a Client Money Account "as prescribed under COB 8". The intended scheme follows from these rules. But COB 8.2.1, the heading of COB 8.2 ("Client Money: Investment Business") and the Glossary definition of "Client Money" still describe only Money held in connection with Investment Business, so the definition and the heading do not match the rule that applies them.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0086 — COB 8.5 was extended to Insurance Managers but the distribution waterfall and agency rule still name only the Insurance Intermediary
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 2 rewrote the old COB 11.8 as COB 8.5 for "an Insurance Intermediary or Insurance Manager", and that phrase runs through COB 8.5. Three places still name only the Insurance Intermediary: 8.5.15(2)(c) "where insufficient funds are held by the Insurance Intermediary"; 8.5.15(2)(d)(i) "trustee in bankruptcy over the Insurance Intermediary, payment must be made accordance with the AIFC Insolvency Regulations"; and 8.5.5(b) "once the money is received by the Insurance Intermediary". The Investment Business rule 8.2.16(2)(d)(i) covers "the Authorised Firm or the Nominee Company".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0085 — COB 2.3.1(b) lists only COB 2.5.1 and 2.5.5 and omits Undertakings assessed under COB 2.5.6
entry.summary: Reported. COB 2.3.1(b) allows a Person to be classified as a Professional Client if it meets the requirements to be an Assessed Professional Client "in accordance with COB 2.5.1 or 2.5.5". COB 2.5.1 covers individuals and 2.5.5 joint account holders. COB 2.5.6 (Undertakings with own funds of at least USD 1 million) is not listed, although 2.5.6 itself applies "For the purposes of COB 2.3.1" and the Glossary defines Assessed Professional Client by "COB 2.5.1 and 2.5.6". The words of 2.5.6 and the Glossary keep the intended meaning, but the list in 2.3.1(b) does not match them.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0084 — COB 1.2.4 lists 'COB 15 (Record Keeping)' for Trust Service Providers: COB 15 is complaints, record keeping is COB 16
entry.summary: Reported. COB 1.2.4 disapplies COB to Trust Service Providers except, among others, "COB 15 (Record Keeping)". Chapter 15 is "Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution"; Chapter 16 is "Record Keeping and Internal Audit"; and section 15.4 inside Chapter 15 is "Record keeping" for complaints. The number and the label point to different provisions. The mismatch exists from the first version of COB (2017) and was kept through every later change to 1.2.4. Other exclusion rules name the chapters correctly, for example 1.2.2(g): "COB 15 (Complaints Handling and Dispute Resolution), COB 16 (Record Keeping and Internal Audit)".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0083 — COB 13.2.10 heading in the consolidated texts and online reads "Principle 8 ‐ Client Money and Client Assets"; Amendments No. 11 inserted "Principle 10 – Complaints"
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 11 (in force 1 January 2024) inserted COB 13.2.9 "Principle 9 ‐ Conflicts of interest" and 13.2.10 "Principle 10 – Complaints"; the amending instrument shows both headings as new text. The consolidated versions V12 to V17 on aifc.kz and the AFSA online COB show 13.2.10 under the heading "Principle 8 ‐ Client Money and Client Assets", which is the heading of 13.2.8. The rulebook therefore has two "Principle 8" headings and no Principle 10. The text of 13.2.10 itself (complaints) is correct.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0082 — COB 15.5.4 points to 'paragraph 2 of COB 15.4.2', a one-paragraph rule on the content of complaint records
entry.summary: Reported. COB 15.5.4 requires information about other means of resolving complaints, "as outlined in paragraph 2 of COB 15.4.2", to be made available on the website, at branches and in the client terms of a Money Service Provider. COB 15.4.2 ("Content of records") has a single paragraph on what a complaints record must contain; it has no paragraph 2. The duty to inform a complainant of other means of resolving the Complaint is the second paragraph of COB 15.2.5. The wrong number is already in Amendments No. 14, which inserted COB 15.5.4. The descriptive words keep the meaning.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0081 — COB 19.5.1(c): the Insurer's claims item has no operative words
entry.summary: Reported. COB 19.5.1(c) reads only "(including by terminating or avoiding a policy); and": there is no verb and no object. The parallel lists for Insurance Intermediaries (COB 11.7.6(c)) and Insurance Managers (COB 20.4.1(c)) read "not unreasonably reject a claim (including by terminating or avoiding a policy); and". Both the amending instrument and the consolidated text show the item with nothing before the parenthesis; it is already incomplete in Amendments No. 2 (2 December 2018), which inserted COB 19. The general claims-handling duty in 19.5.1(a) still applies.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0080 — AFSA online COB does not include the Amendments No. 14 changes in force since 13 January 2026
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 14 to COB commence on 13 January 2026, except the changes to COB 1.2.2, which commenced on 13 October 2025. The consolidated version V17 on aifc.kz contains them: COB 8.1.2 and 8.1.4 now cover firms that Provide Money Services, the Guidance under COB 8.2.5 refers to PMS 9, COB 15.1 has two new paragraphs, and the new COB 15.5 sets a deadline of 15 business days for Money Service complaints. The aifc.kz page for COB says that the current version can be found on the regulator's website. The AFSA online COB (checked on 23 October 2026) shows none of these changes: COB 8.1.2(a) still refers only to Investment Business, COB 15.1 has one paragraph, and there is no COB 15.5. The page shows no deleted (struck-through) text at these places.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0079 — aifc.kz, The Structure of the Bodies of the AIFC: two links serve the wrong file
entry.summary: Reported. The links "… ru (initial)" and "… with amendments as of 9 October 2017. ENG" serve the same file as the 2021 Russian consolidation ("с изменениями и дополнениями по состоянию на 1 июля 2021 года"). The initial Russian text and the 2017 English version are not available.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0078 — AFSA online rulebook: the page "Financial Services Exempt from Corporate Tax" carries no act title, number, date or adopting body
entry.summary: Reported. The page is listed under Rules (version 1 January 2020) and states that a participant "shall not be liable for corporation tax … on income or capital" for the services in its Schedule 1. It carries no act title, number, date or adopting body, no end date (the Statute sets 1 January 2066) and no exclusion of the digital asset exchange (Article 6(3), since 2023).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0077 — The Structure of the Bodies of the AIFC, §9(14): the Governor recommends judges "to the Council"
entry.summary: Reported. Under Article 13(3-1) of the Constitutional Statute the Chairman and judges of the AIFC Court are appointed by the President on the Governor's recommendation; the AIFC Court Regulations say the same. §9(14) of the Structure of the Bodies (as of 1 July 2021) says that the Governor recommends to the Council the persons to be appointed as judges, wording that predates the 2017 amendment of the Statute.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0074 — aifc.kz: the link "Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan kz" opens the Constitution of Kazakhstan
