entry.summary: Reported. On the Constitutional Statute page of aifc.kz the link labelled "Constitutional Statute of the Republic of Kazakhstan kz" serves constitution-of-the-rk-kz.pdf, a 48-page Kazakh text of the Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0072 — PRU (Investment Firms) 3.2: the definition of Capital Resources refers three times to "the Insurance Intermediary"
entry.summary: Reported. Rule 3.2(1)(a) counts the share capital "of the PRU Investment Firm", but 3.2(1)(c) counts retained earnings and reserves "of the Insurance Intermediary", and the deductions in 3.2(2)(b)(iv) and (v) refer to the pension fund assets and own shares of "the Insurance Intermediary". The intended meaning is clear from context, but the text names a different kind of firm. The Prudential Rules for Insurance Intermediaries now say "the Authorised Firm" in the same items.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0071 — PRU (Investment Firms) 1.3(10) and 6.1(2): which Chapter 6 rules apply to Externally Regulated firms
entry.summary: Reported. Rule 1.3(10) says that "in Chapter 6, only Rule 6.6 applies" to Externally Regulated PRU Investment Firms. Rule 6.1(2) says "Other than Rules 6.5 and 6.6, this Chapter does not apply" to them, and Rule 6.5(2) contains a limitation written for them. Rule 6.5 carries the duty to notify a breach within one Business Day and the restriction on payments to Affiliates, so whether these firms are bound by it depends on which rule is read.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0070 — PRU (Investment Firms) Table 3.3: a manager of a Single Family Office Fund without a custodian falls in two rows (USD 50,000 and USD 500,000)
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 4 (in force 1 July 2024) added "or (b) because the Fund is a Single Family Office Fund" to the USD 50,000 row of Table 3.3. The USD 500,000 row for a Collective Investment Scheme "which does not have an appointed Eligible Custodian" was not changed; its only exception is the nature of the Fund and its assets. A manager of a Single Family Office Fund without an Eligible Custodian therefore meets both rows, and the text does not say which applies. Reading both rows cumulatively gives USD 500,000 and leaves the limb added by Amendments No. 4 without effect.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0069 — Glossary, "Authorised Investment Exchange": refers to "Operating an Investment Exchange"
entry.summary: Reported. The definition refers to the "Market Activity of Operating an Investment Exchange". The Market Activity in GEN Schedule 4, paragraph 1, and in the Glossary itself is "Operating an Exchange". The entry "Operating a facility for Investment Tokens" uses the same name.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0068 — Glossary, "Approved Individual": the two limbs are joined by "and"
entry.summary: Reported. An Approved Individual is defined as an individual "(1) approved by the AFSA to carry out a Controlled Function; and (2) approved by the AFSA to be appointed by a DNFBP and Registered Auditor to carry out the MLRO function". Read literally, an individual approved only for a Controlled Function is not an Approved Individual. Section 21 of the Framework Regulations defines the term by limb (1) alone. The AFSA online Glossary shows both versions: the list has the two limbs, the term page only limb (1).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0067 — Glossary: three insurance client money terms point to COB 11.8, which no longer exists
entry.summary: Reported. "Client Money Distribution Rules" ("COB 11.8.14"), "Client Money" ("COB 11.8.4") and "Segregated Client" ("COB 11.8") point to COB 11.8. Chapter 11 of the current COB ends at 11.7; the client money rules for insurance intermediation are in COB 8.5 (including 8.5.5, money held as agent of an insurer, and 8.5.15, distribution rules). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0005 changes the fourth such entry, "Insurance Intermediary Audit Report", to refer to GEN 6.3.9, which we support, but leaves these three as they are.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0066 — Glossary, "Money Services": excludes activities "specified in paragraph 21 (3)" of GEN Schedule 1, which does not exist
entry.summary: Reported. The definition, adopted with Amendments No. 21 (in force 13 October 2025), excludes "any of the activities specified in paragraph 21 (3) Schedule 1 of GEN". Paragraph 21 has no sub-paragraph (3); the same package of amendments moved the exclusions to paragraph 21-1.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0065 — Glossary, "Operating a Loan Crowdfunding Platform": points to Schedule 3 of the Framework Regulations, which no longer exists
entry.summary: Reported. The entry reads "The Market Activity as defined in paragraph 4 of Schedule 3 of the Framework Regulations". Market Activities moved to Schedule 4 of the General Rules (Framework Regulations section 18(1)); the neighbouring entries were updated, this one was not.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0064 — Glossary, "Takaful Business": points to paragraph 24 of GEN Schedule 1 (Insurance Management)
entry.summary: Reported. The Glossary defines Takaful Business as "A Regulated Activity defined in paragraph 24 of Schedule 1 of the GEN". Paragraph 24 is Insurance Management; Takaful Business is paragraph 25.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0063 — Glossary, "Money Laundering Reporting Officer": points to GEN 2.3.4, which is omitted
entry.summary: Reported. The Glossary defines the MLRO as "the individual performing the Designated Function identified at GEN 2.3.4". GEN 2.3.4 now reads "[intentionally omitted]"; the MLRO is a Controlled Function under GEN 2.2.5-1 and must be held by an Approved Individual (GEN 2.1.1(1)(d)).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0062 — GEN 2.2.1 and 2.3.1: the ranges of Controlled and Designated Functions are out of date
entry.summary: Reported. GEN 2.2.1 says "The functions specified in GEN 2.2.2 to 2.2.5 are Controlled Functions", but the MLRO function is now GEN 2.2.5-1. GEN 2.3.1 says "The functions specified in GEN 2.3.2 to 2.3.4 are Designated Functions", but 2.3.4 is omitted and the Risk Manager and Internal Audit Manager functions are 2.3.5 and 2.3.6.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0061 — GEN Schedule 4, paragraph 5(5)(c): the investment crowdfunding delegation rule requires notice to "Borrowers or lenders"
entry.summary: Reported. Paragraph 5(5)(c) (Operating an Investment Crowdfunding Platform) repeats paragraph 4(5)(c) of the loan crowdfunding definition: the delegate must "notify Borrowers or lenders". Paragraph 5 otherwise speaks of Issuers and Investors; for shares and other non-debt investments there is no Borrower or lender to notify.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0060 — GEN 6.2.4(7)(b) borrows procedures and powers from Rule 6.2.4(6), which lists only factors
entry.summary: Reported. For a branch Bank without a home notification requirement, the first sentence of GEN 6.2.4(7)(b) applies the requirements of (4); the next words say the AFSA "must follow the same procedures, and shall have the same powers, as set out in Rule 6.2.4 (6)". Rule 6.2.4(6) is a list of factors; the procedure is in (4) and the power to object in (5).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0059 — GEN 2.2.7 refers to requirements made under section 43(1) of the Framework Regulations; the matching waiver power is section 42(2)
entry.summary: Reported. GEN 2.2.7 lets a firm apply to waive "requirements made pursuant to Section 43(1)" in the light of a foreign registration or approval. Section 43(1) is the fit-and-proper criterion; the provision with the same wording about foreign approval is section 42(2), which allows waiving the requirements as to form and content under section 42(1).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0058 — GEN 6.1.4 refers to "the contract required under GEN 6.1.2"; the contract is required by GEN 6.1.3
entry.summary: Reported. GEN 6.1.4 (lead-in, (b) and (e)) sets the terms of "the contract required under GEN 6.1.2". GEN 6.1.2 names and nominates the Skilled Person; the written contract is required by GEN 6.1.3.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0057 — GEN 1.3.3-1 cites section 41(1) of the Framework Regulations, which sets only a fit-and-proper criterion
entry.summary: Reported. GEN 1.3.3-1 assesses whether an Ancillary Service Provider can be effectively supervised "for the purposes of section 41(1) of the Framework Regulations". Section 41(1) contains only the fit-and-proper criterion, while for Authorised Firms the effective supervision criterion is a separate item (section 34(1)(c)).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0056 — GEN Guidance after 1.1.2 cites section 32(4) of the Framework Regulations; section 32 has no subsections
entry.summary: Reported. The Guidance refers to a waiver "pursuant to section 32(4) of the Framework Regulations". Section 32 (Financial technology) is a single paragraph; the power to waive requirements as to form and content is section 31(4).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0055 — AFSA online rulebook, GEN 4.3.2: the integrity principle is printed under the heading of Principle 2
entry.summary: Reported. In GEN V20 (aifc.kz) 4.3.2 requires each Approved Individual and Designated Individual to "act with due skill, care and diligence". On the AFSA online rulebook the text under "4.3.2. Principle 2 - Due skill, care and diligence" is the integrity sentence of 4.3.1, so the due skill principle for individuals is missing online.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0054 — GEN 2.2.9: the duty on an Approved Individual leaving binds only "the Authorised Firm"
entry.summary: Reported. GEN 2.2.9 is triggered when an Approved Individual ceases to be employed "by an Authorised Person", but the duty to request withdrawal of the status within seven days and to report the reasons falls on "the Authorised Firm". An Authorised Person also includes an Authorised Market Institution, to which GEN 2 applies, so no one is bound when an Authorised Market Institution's Approved Individual leaves. Paragraph (b) of the same rule already says "the Authorised Person".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0053 — GEN Schedule 1, paragraph 4(2): two activity names that do not exist
entry.summary: Reported. Paragraph 4(2) incorporates into Managing a Collective Investment Scheme activities constituting "Dealing as Agent" and "Dealing as Principal". Schedule 1 defines "Dealing in Investments as Agent" (paragraph 2) and "Dealing in Investments as Principal" (paragraph 1); the Glossary does not define the two shorter names. The wording has been there since the initial 2017 release. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0001 (Annex 2) corrects a third name in the same paragraph ("Managing Assets" to "Managing Investments") but keeps these two.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0052 — FEES: several fees and payment terms are set in "Notes" and footnotes, which are not part of an AIFC Act
entry.summary: Reported. Section 26(1)(a) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts says that "a footnote, endnote or other note" is not part of an AIFC Act, even if inserted by an amending act (section 26(2)). In FEES the application fee for change of control (1 400 USD), the Approved Individual fee (500 USD), the quarterly payment of variable fees and the deferral of some fees to 1 January 2027 appear under "Notes" headings or in footnotes.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0051 — Variable fees: the payment deadline can expire before the invoice is issued
entry.summary: Reported. Variable fees are "paid within 21 days after the issuance of an invoice by the AFSA, but no later than within 1 month following each corresponding quarter". If the invoice is issued late in the following month, or after it, the payer may have fewer than 21 days or the deadline may precede the invoice, and the 1% per month increase under FEES 5.1.2 can start before the invoice arrives.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0050 — FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Dealing in Investments as Agent): "assets under brokerage" is not defined
entry.summary: Reported. The quarterly levy of 0.0005% applies to "the amount of the assets under brokerage" above 490 million USD. The term is not defined in FEES or in the Glossary, and it is not used in any other AFSA rulebook, so it is unclear whether it means client assets held in brokerage accounts or the volume executed.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0049 — aifc.kz: the Fees Rules page does not link Amendments No. 12 (1 May 2022)
entry.summary: Reported. The list of amending instruments on the Fees Rules page goes from A11 to A13. Amendments No. 12 (approved 24 April 2022, in force 1 May 2022), which introduced the annual supervision fees, late fees and FinTech Lab fees, is in the site's media library but is not linked from the page.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0048 — Fees Rules V15: cover date "as of 9 December 2022" is that of V14; two instruments numbered 14.1
entry.summary: Reported. The cover of V15 and its label on aifc.kz read "with amendments as of 9 December 2022", the date already used for V14. The instruments consolidated in V15 are dated 10 September 2023, 10 September 2023 and 9 December 2023, and two of them are both numbered "Amendments No. 14.1".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0047 — FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Providing Money Services, from 2027): measurement period of the "annual transaction value" is not set
entry.summary: Reported. From 1 January 2027 the variable fee is "calculated on a quarterly basis", but both the threshold (280 million USD) and the base are "the annual transaction value" at "0.0015% p.a.". The text does not say which year's value is used at each quarter or how quarterly charges and any year-end adjustment are worked out. The deferral to 2027 is in a footnote, which is not part of an AIFC Act (section 26 of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0046 — FEES 1.2.5(a), 1.2.6(a) and Schedule 7 refer to each other; no amount is set
entry.summary: Reported. FEES 1.2.5(a) and 1.2.6(a) charge "the application fees specified in Schedule 7", and Schedule 7 says that the Chief Executive Officer "may determine the amount of fee specified in 1.2.5 (a) and 1.2.6.(a)". No amount appears in the Rules themselves, while section 9(7) of the Framework Regulations speaks of a fee "prescribed in the Rules".

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0045 — FEES Schedules 10 and 11: no start date and no cap for the daily surcharge on unpaid late fees
entry.summary: Reported. "Non-payment of the late fee within 30 calendar days incurs a further late payment fee equal to 10% of the late fee for each calendar day" (5% in Schedule 11). The text does not say from which day the 30 days run (the contravention, the end of the 3 or 5 business days, or an invoice) and sets no cap on the surcharge (the AFSA may waive fees under FEES 5.1.3).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0044 — FEES 4.1.2 still says the fee for extracts will be set "at a later date"
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 6 (27 December 2019) made the fee in FEES 4.1.1 one "specified in Schedule 5-1" (the "Processing inquiries" row), but left FEES 4.1.2: "The Registrar of Companies may determine the amount of the fee specified in FEES 4.1.1 at a later date."

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0043 — FEES Schedule 1, table 1.2: footnote marker "Fee (USD)*" without a footnote
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 17 deleted both the asterisk and the footnote of the modification fee tables in Schedules 1, 2 and 3. V18 and the online rulebook removed the footnote everywhere and the asterisk in Schedules 2 and 3, but kept "Fee (USD)*" in Schedule 1, table 1.2.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0042 — FEES 3.1.2 and 3.1.4(b): the initial supervision fee runs from "the grant of the Licence", which recognised Non-AIFC bodies never receive
entry.summary: Reported. Before Amendments No. 17 the due date ran from "the commencement of operations", which fitted every payer. Since then the initial annual supervision fee is due "within 21 days of the date of the grant of the Licence" and is pro-rated from that date. FEES 3.1.1 also makes Recognised Non-AIFC Market Institutions and Members pay the fee, but they are recognised by an order under the Framework Regulations, not licensed under Part 3, so the specific due date and the pro-rating do not fit them.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0041 — FEES Schedule 1, 1.1-1: the exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility is printed but was never enacted
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 14.1 (9 December 2023) inserted 1.1-1 (additional application fee for Digital Assets activities) without an exception; the same instrument put an exception for Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility only into 6.1-1. Consolidated versions V15 to V18 print the exception in 1.1-1 as well, and we could not find it in any of the published amending instruments Nos. 12 to 17. Whether a Digital Asset Trading Facility applicant owes the additional fee (now 2 800 USD) depends on which text is right; a consolidated version cannot change legal effect (section 19(2) of the AIFC Regulations on AIFC Acts). The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0004 amends 1.1-1 again (the fixed amount is replaced by a table) and prints the words "except for the Regulated Activity of Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility" as existing text, not as an insertion.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0040 — FEES Schedule 6, 6.4: the Recognised Non-AIFC Member trading value fee is ambiguous for members on several platforms
entry.summary: Reported. The trading value fee applies to members "whose trading value is over 25 million USD per quarter on each trading platform". For a member above the threshold on one platform and below it on another, the text can mean that no fee is due (not over the threshold on each platform) or that a fee is due per platform; the base ("0.001% of trading value") does not say whether it is per platform or in total.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0039 — FEES 1.3 refers to Schedule 6 for Approved Individual application fees; Schedule 6 has none
entry.summary: Reported. FEES 1.3 says Approved Individual fees are "as specified in Schedules 1, 2 or 6". Schedule 6 sets annual supervision fees only. Approved Individual fees are in Schedules 1 and 2, in Schedule 3 (change of MLRO, Audit Principal) and in Schedule 8 (FinTech Lab, 200 USD). Amendments No. 12 replaced "3 or 4" with "or 6" in 2022.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0038 — FEES Schedule 6, table 6.2 (crowdfunding platforms): no rule for funds raised of exactly 1 million USD
entry.summary: Reported. The variable fee is "not applicable" where "the funds raised is less than 1 million USD", and a levy applies to the whole amount where "the funds raised is more than 1 million USD". Funds raised of exactly 1 million USD in a quarter are covered by no branch, while the outcomes on either side differ. The draft in Consultation Paper AFSA-PSRD-CSP-2026-0004 raises the threshold to 5.3, 5.5 and 5.8 million USD for 2027, 2028 and 2029 with the same wording ("less than" and "more than"), so the gap moves to those amounts.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0037 — FEES Schedule 6, table 6.1 (Digital Asset Trading Facility): no rule for an average daily trading value of exactly 500 000 USD
entry.summary: Reported. The variable fee is "not applicable" where the average daily trading value is "less than 500 000 USD" and is the greater of the trading levy and 5 000 USD where it is "more than 500 000 USD". A value of exactly 500 000 USD is covered by no branch, while the outcomes on either side differ (0 USD and at least 5 000 USD for the quarter).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0036 — FEES Schedule 8, 8.6: the consolidated text omits words adopted by Amendments No. 17
entry.summary: Reported. Amendments No. 17 (13 November 2025) inserted 8.6 as "50% of an application fee for change of control payable under Schedule 1 of FEES". The consolidated V18 and the AFSA online rulebook omit "for change of control". The heading of 8.6 still ties the fee to change of control, so the meaning survives, but the published body text differs from the adopted one.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0035 — AML Guidance refers to Chapter 6 for risk assessments; they are in Chapters 4 and 5
entry.summary: Reported. Guidance (k) after AML 4.3.3 and Guidance (j) after AML 6.3.4 refer to the customer risk assessment "under Chapter 6", and the sanctions Guidance (g) to "the risk assessments under Chapters 5 and 6". AML 1.5(d) places the customer risk assessment in Chapter 5; Chapter 6 contains none.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0034 — AML Guidance after 13.1.3 cites GEN 2.1.2 for the MLRO appointment; it is now GEN 2.1.1(1)(d)
entry.summary: Reported. The Guidance says "Under GEN 2.1.2., the MLRO function is a mandatory appointment." In the current General Rules GEN 2.1.2(1) is omitted and the MLRO appointment is GEN 2.1.1(1)(d).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0033 — AML 2.2(d) and Annex 1 define "senior management" differently
entry.summary: Reported. AML 2.2(d) says that "In these Rules 'senior management' means" every member of executive management, including every member of the Governing Body. Annex 1, which AML 1.6 names as the place of definitions, defines it as "a high-level executive who oversees the operations and performance of one or more departments". Responsibility under 2.2(a) and approvals for politically exposed persons depend on which definition applies.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0032 — AML: the online rulebook named as the current version differs from the aifc.kz text of 15 December 2024
entry.summary: Reported. aifc.kz offers the AML Rules "with amendments as of 15 December 2024, which commence on 1 January 2025" and says the current version is on the regulator's website. The AFSA online rulebook (as displayed on 23 October 2026) dates its AML articles 12 December 2021 (Chapter 11-1: 4 January 2024) and differs in binding rules: 6.6.1(d) reads "terminate or suspend" instead of "terminate"; 4.3.2(e) (transactions aimed at cashing out money obtained by criminal means) is missing; 5.1.5 prints its second paragraph twice and lacks the first paragraph. The amending instrument of 15 December 2024 is not published.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0031 — AML 14.2.3(b) refers to the staff training rule AML 14.1.1(b)
entry.summary: Reported. AML 14.2.3 deals with Group entities, but (b) requires the firm to document "the basis for its satisfaction that the requirement in AML 14.1.1.(b) is met" — the rule on training the firm's own employees. The intended target is probably AML 14.2.1(b) or the equivalence test in AML 14.2.2.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0030 — AML 14.1.1(i): training on findings "described in Chapter 13"; the findings are in Chapter 12
entry.summary: Reported. AML 14.1.1(i) requires employees to understand the relevant findings, recommendations and directives "described in Chapter 13". They are defined in Chapter 12 (12.2.1), and the parallel MLRO duty in 13.6.1(g) correctly refers to Chapter 12.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0029 — AML 13.6.1(b), 13.8.1, 13.8.2, 14.1.1(d)–(e), 14.5.1(c): references to "AML 13.7.3" now point to the wrong rule
entry.summary: Reported. Seven references to "a notification to the MLRO under AML 13.7.3" survive from the 2018 numbering. AML 13.7.3 is now "Suspicious Activity and Transactions Controls" and creates no notification; the employee's duty to report to the MLRO is AML 13.7.5. The MLRO's duties to enquire, to decide on a suspicious transaction report, to record reasons and to keep records are attached to the old number.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0028 — CIBS art. L. 312-37 on Légifrance, version from 1 February to 1 August 2026: no « Modifié par » link to the 2026 Finance Act
entry.summary: Corrected. The version of article L. 312-37 of the Code of taxes on goods and services in force from 1 February 2026 to 1 August 2026 (LEGIARTI000053593049) carries the amount of €19.24 set by Article 71, I, 4°, d, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act), and its note refers to V of that article. Yet the version has no « Modifié par » link to that law, while the following versions of the same article (LEGIARTI000053592986, LEGIARTI000053593023) do. The text of the version is correct; only the link to the amending law is missing.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0027 — Rev. Proc. 2025-32: the 2026 section 6334(d)(4)(B) amount is published as $5,300; the statutory rounding rule gives $5,250
entry.summary: Reported. Section 6334(d)(4)(C) increases the $4,150 amount by the cost-of-living adjustment (base year 2017) and rounds the increase down to a multiple of $100. For 2026 the increase is $1,167.12, rounded to $1,100, giving $5,250. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 publishes $5,300 in section 4.50 (wages exempt from levy) and section 4.35 (qualified disability trust deduction, which uses the same adjustment); the published increase, $1,150, is not a multiple of $100 and matches rounding the full amount, $5,317.12, down. Rev. Proc. 2024-40 shows the same pattern for 2025 in sections 2.35 and 2.51: $5,100 published, $5,150 under the statute.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0025 — Rev. Proc. 2025-32: the 2026 head-of-household standard deduction is published as $24,150; the statutory rounding rule gives $24,175
entry.summary: Reported. Section 63(c)(7)(B)(ii) increases the $23,625 base by the cost-of-living adjustment and rounds the increase down to the next lowest multiple of $50. With the C-CPI-U values published on 11 September 2025 the increase is $559.56, rounded to $550, giving $24,175. Rev. Proc. 2025-32, section 4.14(1), publishes $24,150: its increase of $525 is not a multiple of $50 and matches rounding the whole amount instead of the increase.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0022 — CSS art. L. 162-23-8 on Légifrance, version from 1 September 2027: both changes made by the 2026 social security financing act are missing
entry.summary: Corrected. Article 72, I, 5°, of Law No. 2025-1403 deletes « part prévue au 2° du I de l'article L. 162-23, affectée à la » from the first paragraph of I of article L. 162-23-8 of the Social Security Code and inserts « exerçant les activités mentionnées au 4° du même article L. 162-22 ». The version in force until 1 September 2027 (LEGIARTI000053283299) contains both changes; the version from 1 September 2027 (LEGIARTI000048971734, which stems from Law No. 2023-29) contains none of them and restores the earlier wording. The discrepancy arose in the consolidation; the text published in the Official Journal is correct.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0021 — CGI art. 1600 on Légifrance, version for 2027: the 2026 Finance Act insertion on the Corsica chamber of commerce is missing
entry.summary: Corrected. Article 135, VI, A, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) inserts « et l'établissement public du commerce et de l'industrie de Corse » after « région » in I of article 1600 of the General Tax Code, with no end date. The version published on Légifrance for 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2028 (LEGIARTI000049534935) does not contain the insertion, while the preceding version (from 1 March 2026) and the versions for 2028 to 2030 do. The discrepancy arose in the consolidation; the text published in the Official Journal is correct.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0020 — CSS art. L. 136-4, IV, on Légifrance: the word « aux » dropped and « définiaux » run together after the 2026 social security financing act
entry.summary: Accepted by the addressee. We applied article 18, I, 2°, of Law No. 2025-1403 to the prior consolidated version of article L. 136-4, IV, of the Social Security Code and compared the result with the versions published on Légifrance (LEGIARTI000053282498 from 31 December 2025 and LEGIARTI000053284767 in force since 21 February 2026). The instruction replaces only « mêmes articles 64 bis et 76 », so the result reads « déterminés aux articles 50-0, 64 bis, 76 et 102 ter » and « du champ défini aux articles »; both versions read « déterminés articles » and « définiaux ». The discrepancy arose in the consolidation; the text published in the Official Journal is correct.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0024 — Rabbit grading, paragraph 10: the Russian and Kazakh texts set opposite culling conditions
entry.summary: Reported. The Russian text of paragraph 10 recommends culling does “that raised fewer than 5 kits in each of the first two kindlings” and those with “more than two consecutive misses”. The Kazakh text of the same paragraph names does that raised “at least 5 kits” and misses “twice in a row”. The condition on the number of kits is reversed between the language versions, and the number of misses differs.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0023 — 2026 energy taxation guide: the ED95 rate is 12.119 €/MWh on page 25 but 12.157 €/MWh on pages 33 and 37
entry.summary: Reported. We compared the « Guide 2026 sur la fiscalité des énergies » published by the Ministry of Ecological Transition (editions of 30 May and 22 July 2026) with article L. 312-79 of the Code of taxes on goods and services (CIBS). Page 25 and article L. 312-79 give 12.119 €/MWh for ethanol-diesel ED95, while page 33 (annex 2) and page 37 (annex 3, 6.43 €/hL) give 12.157 €/MWh, although 6.43 × 3.6 / 1.91 = 12.119. The discrepancy is in the guide; the rate in the code is not affected.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0019 — LF 2026 art. 81, V: « code général des collectivité territoriales » (missing plural in the name of the code)
entry.summary: Reported. Article 81, V, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) introduces amendments to « La deuxième partie du code général des collectivité territoriales ». The code is the « code général des collectivités territoriales », as the same article writes it elsewhere. The final text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 227) carries the same spelling, so the discrepancy is in the adopted text; the code referred to remains identifiable.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0018 — LFSS 2026 art. 102, II, 3°: the title of Law No. 2025-199 misquoted as « de financement pour la sécurité sociale »
entry.summary: Reported. Article 102, II, 3°, of Law No. 2025-1403 (2026 social security financing act) cites « la loi n° 2025-199 du 28 février 2025 de financement pour la sécurité sociale pour 2025 ». The exact title, « de financement de la sécurité sociale pour 2025 », appears in IX of the same article. The text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 199 rect.) carries the same words, so the discrepancy is in the adopted text; the law referred to remains identifiable.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0017 — LFSS 2026 art. 12, II, 1°: Law No. 2016-1918 cited as a « financement » amending act instead of the amending finance act for 2016
entry.summary: Reported. Article 12, II, 1°, of Law No. 2025-1403 (2026 social security financing act) refers to « la loi n° 2016-1918 du 29 décembre 2016 de financement rectificative pour 2016 ». In the LEGI register of texts, Law No. 2016-1918 of 29 December 2016 is the amending finance act for 2016 (« de finances rectificative pour 2016 »). The text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 199 rect.) carries the same words, so the discrepancy is in the adopted text; the law referred to remains identifiable by its number and date.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0016 — LF 2026 art. 183, II: Law No. 2020-1721 cited with the date 9 December 2020 instead of 29 December 2020
entry.summary: Reported. Article 183, II, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) amends article 225 of « la loi n° 2020-1721 du 9 décembre 2020 de finances pour 2021 ». Law No. 2020-1721 is dated 29 December 2020, and other articles of the same act, such as article 19, cite it with that date. The final text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 227) carries the same date, so the discrepancy is in the adopted text; the law referred to remains identifiable by its number.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0015 — CGI art. 199 sexdecies: the 2026 Finance Act replaces words that occur twice without saying which occurrence
entry.summary: Reported. We applied article 29, 2°, of Law No. 2026-103 (2026 Finance Act) to the prior consolidated text of article 199 sexdecies of the General Tax Code. Point a) inserts a second occurrence of the words « de l'article D. 7231-1 du même code »; point b) then replaces those words with « du même II » without saying which occurrence, and the sentence in force refers to services « mentionnés au 16° du II du même II ». The discrepancy is in the adopted text itself: the final text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 227) and the authenticated Official Journal No. 0043 carry the same wording.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0014 — LFSS 2026 art. 99, V, 4° b and c, and 6°: the published text omitted « first occurrence » where the anchor word occurs twice (corrected on 23 May 2026)
entry.summary: Corrected before our report. As published in the Official Journal of 31 December 2025, three insertions in article 99, V, of Law No. 2025-1403 were placed « après le mot : « enfant » » (7° and 8° of article L. 223-1 of the Social Security Code) and « après le mot : « travail » » (1° of article L. 351-3), while each word occurs twice in the provision amended. The text adopted by the National Assembly (T.A. No. 199 rect.) reads « après la première occurrence du mot », so the discrepancy arose at publication. The rectificatif published in Official Journal No. 0120 of 23 May 2026 had already restored the adopted wording before Arxo's check of 22 October 2026.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0013 — LFSS 2026 art. 18, II: the 2026 Finance Act cited under the number and date of the social security financing act itself (corrected on 23 May 2026)
entry.summary: Corrected before our report. As published in the Official Journal of 31 December 2025, article 18, II, of Law No. 2025-1403 (2026 social security financing act) referred to « la loi n° 2025-1403 du 30 décembre 2025 de finances pour 2026 », that is, to the 2026 Finance Act under the number and date of Law No. 2025-1403 itself. The text adopted by the National Assembly left the number and date blank, so the discrepancy arose at publication. The rectificatif published in Official Journal No. 0120 of 23 May 2026 had already corrected it before Arxo's check of 22 October 2026.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0010 — Camel grading, paragraph 23: the Russian electronic publication shows the word “ФОРМУЛА” instead of the live-weight formula
entry.summary: Reported. In the Russian card of the Әділет legal information system, paragraph 23 of the grading instructions for camels reads “by the formula: ФОРМУЛА”: the word “FORMULA” stands where the formula should be. The Kazakh card shows an image of the formula at the same place.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0009 — Maral and sika deer grading, paragraph 20: the weight threshold for class III hinds is “(ISO-IBS kg)” instead of a number
entry.summary: Reported. Paragraph 20 of the grading instructions for marals and sika deer assigns to class III the hinds “with a very low live weight (ISO-IBS kg)”: a placeholder stands where the weight should be. Class II is 170–184 kg, so a hind below 170 kg cannot be classed by weight. The Russian and Kazakh texts read the same way.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0008 — Beef cattle grading, paragraph 28: class I is written as “81-70 points”, so totals of 61–70 fall into no class
entry.summary: Reported. Paragraph 28 of the grading instructions for beef cattle sets “elite – 71-80 points”, “class I – 81-70 points” and “class II – 51-60 points”. A total of 61 to 70 points matches no row: a cow scoring 65 receives no class for the complex of traits. The Russian and Kazakh texts read the same way.

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0002 — Instructions for Form 6251 (2025) cite 26 U.S.C. §56(b)(5)(D), which does not exist
entry.summary: Reported. The 2025 Instructions for Form 6251 say the enhanced deduction for seniors is treated as a personal exemption and added back to alternative minimum taxable income “as an adjustment under section 56(b)(5)(D)”. Section 56(b) has no paragraph (5); the disallowance of personal exemptions is in section 56(b)(1)(D).

entry.title: ARXO-2026-0001 — P.L. 119-21 §70204(a)(2)(A) quotes words that are not in 26 U.S.C. §529A(b)(2)(B)
entry.summary: Reported. The amending instruction inserts new words after “except as provided in the case of contributions under subsection (c)(1)(C)”. Section 529A(b)(2)(B) reads “except in the case of contributions under subsection (c)(1)(C)”: the quoted words do not occur, as written in 2014 and kept in later amendments. The Office of the Law Revision Counsel executed the insertion after the existing words to reflect the probable intent of Congress.
